payload.title: Review TASK-3288
_run_subprocess buffers full output in memory before bounding it
payload.body: _run_subprocess (complexity_collectors.py) calls proc.communicate() with no read-size limit, then truncates to max_output_bytes only after the full stdout/stderr have been buffered in memory. A pathological or malicious subprocess (e.g. a Ruff/wiki CLI invocation against an adversarial input) can exhaust memory before the truncation ever applies, defeating the bound's purpose. Fix: read from proc.stdout/proc.stderr in bounded chunks (e.g. via StreamReader.read(n) in a loop) and stop/kill the process once max_output_bytes is reached, instead of communicate()+slice. Needs new tests covering large-output truncation and process reaping when the bound is hit before EOF. Found during FEAT-561's second-pass adversarial code review; not fixed there because a correct bounded-read rewrite needs its own test coverage.

payload.title: COMPLEXITY_ERROR_CODES has no assertion it stays a subset of models.ERROR_CODES
payload.body: complexity_models.py keeps a local COMPLEXITY_ERROR_CODES frozenset (deliberately not imported from models.py to avoid an import cycle), but there is no test asserting COMPLEXITY_ERROR_CODES <= ERROR_CODES, so the two sets can silently drift if either is edited independently. Suggestion: add a cheap unit test (not a runtime import) that pulls both sets and asserts the subset relationship. SUGGESTION-level finding from FEAT-561's second-pass code review; not fixed per no-scope-creep (do NOT fix SUGGESTION findings).

payload.title: ComplexityAssessment freeze semantics rely on a validator, not frozen=True
payload.body: ComplexityAssessment uses a _freeze_evidence model_validator(mode='after') to defensively copy/freeze its evidence field rather than declaring the model frozen=True (or the field itself immutable via a frozen sub-model config). This works but is a less-obvious pattern than Pydantic's native immutability support, and a future edit that adds a new mutable field could bypass the same protection. SUGGESTION-level finding from FEAT-561's second-pass code review; not fixed per no-scope-creep. Consider standardizing on frozen=True for value objects that must not mutate post-construction.

payload.title: toolkit.py calls a Pydantic classmethod via an instance (cfg.complexity.model_validate(...))
payload.body: SddCoderToolkit.__init__ builds the updated complexity policy as cfg.complexity.model_validate(complexity) -- model_validate is a classmethod, so calling it off the cfg.complexity INSTANCE works but reads as though it validates against that instance, which it does not (it constructs a fresh ComplexityPolicy from complexity ignoring cfg.complexity entirely). Suggestion: call it as type(cfg.complexity).model_validate(complexity) or ComplexityPolicy.model_validate(complexity) for clarity. SUGGESTION-level finding from FEAT-561's second-pass code review; not fixed per no-scope-creep (behavior is correct, only the call-site style is confusing).

payload.title: Malformed-but-present Complexity Contract section silently treated as legacy
payload.body: In parse_complexity_contract's regex-based extraction (_extract_complexity_contract_section, complexity.py), a present '## Complexity Contract' section with the wrong fence language, a missing closing fence, or an empty block fails the extraction regex and falls through to the legacy path (contract_symbols=None, targets from the Files table) instead of raising ComplexityContractError('complexity_contract_invalid'). AC6 calls for a specific diagnostic on invalid structure. Directionally conservative (routes to the same unknown-coverage path a legacy task gets) but loses the specific error the spec wants. Suggested fix: detect a present '## Complexity Contract' heading with no successfully-extracted JSON body and raise complexity_contract_invalid instead of silently falling back.

payload.title: _run_subprocess enforces max_output_bytes only after full buffering, not during capture
payload.body: _run_subprocess (complexity_collectors.py) calls proc.communicate() and buffers the entire stdout/stderr before slicing to policy.max_output_bytes. Spec §7's 8 MiB bound is meant as a capture-time limit, not a post-hoc truncation. Low risk today since inputs are trusted local tooling (ruff/wikitoolkit CLI), not adversarial input, but a pathological subprocess output could still spike memory before truncation. Suggested fix: stream-read with a bounded reader (e.g. asyncio.StreamReader.read(n) in a loop) instead of communicate().

payload.title: models.py ERROR_CODES duplicates complexity_models.py's error code literals instead of importing them
payload.body: models.py's ERROR_CODES re-lists the four complexity error codes (complexity_contract_invalid, complexity_audit_failed, complexity_plan_stale, complex_model_unavailable) as literal strings instead of importing and unioning complexity_models.py's COMPLEXITY_ERROR_CODES, even though models.py already imports the sibling module. Currently in sync but a drift risk: a fifth code added to one and not the other silently diverges. Suggested fix: models.py should do ERROR_CODES = {...} | COMPLEXITY_ERROR_CODES (or equivalent) instead of re-declaring the four strings.

payload.title: engine.py plan()'s complexity_plan_stale except-branch is unreachable
payload.body: In SddCoderEngine.plan()'s per-task loop, 'except CoderFailure as exc: if exc.code == "complexity_plan_stale": raise' is dead code: the loop only calls _compute_assessment, which never raises complexity_plan_stale (only _assessment_for does, and plan() never calls it). Harmless but misleading -- a future reader may assume plan() can surface staleness this way. Suggested fix: remove the branch or add a comment clarifying staleness is only detected in _assessment_for at dispatch time, not during plan().

payload.title: sdd-coder-orchestrator.md scoring table has a copy-paste artifact and describes intended (not fully actual) Ruff syntax-error handling
payload.body: The 'Scoring system' table's Notes column has a copy-paste artifact ('Module (parent directory) count normalized' attached to the wrong row). Separately, the Ruff cyclomatic bullet documents 'Exit code 2, malformed JSON, or syntax errors make that measurement unknown' -- true for exit-2/malformed-JSON via the generic 'returncode not in (0,1)' branch, but the syntax-error case is now handled by a dedicated check for Ruff's 'invalid-syntax' diagnostic code within the exit-1 JSON payload (fixed in FEAT-561's final review pass, complexity_collectors.py's _collect_ruff_cyclomatic) rather than by the generic branch the doc implies. Suggested fix: correct the table row attribution and clarify the syntax-error detection mechanism in the doc.

payload.title: toolkit.py calls ComplexityPolicy.model_validate off a discarded default instance
payload.body: toolkit.py:79 does 'cfg.complexity.model_validate(complexity)' -- model_validate is a classmethod, so calling it off cfg.complexity (a discarded default ComplexityPolicy instance) works but reads misleadingly as if it validates against/mutates that instance. ComplexityPolicy.model_validate(complexity) reads more clearly for the same effect. Purely stylistic, no behavior change.

payload.title: FEAT-558 TOOL_REGISTRY diff reordered ~15 unrelated entries
payload.body: Regenerating scripts/generate_tool_registry.py on a dev that had drifted since the FEAT-558 branch was cut reordered ~15 pre-existing, unrelated TOOL_REGISTRY entries (lyria, o365, tool_optimizations, etc.) with identical key->value pairs, just relocated. Harmless (confirmed via diff: no key added/removed/renamed besides the intended querysource addition) but inflated that PR's diff beyond the minimal querysource change. No action required unless it recurs and becomes a recurring diff-noise pattern worth investigating in the generator itself (e.g. non-deterministic directory scan order).

payload.title: build_conditions forced_conditions can push querylimit above max_rows
payload.body: dialect.py's build_conditions() merges the operator-supplied forced_conditions dict LAST (by design, matching permanent_filter precedence), so if an operator's forced_conditions includes 'querylimit' it can override the toolkit's own max_rows cap. Not LLM-exploitable (forced_conditions is constructor-only config, never an agent-facing argument) and frame_to_result still caps the RETURNED rows via head(max_rows) regardless, so this is a QuerySource-side over-fetch at worst, not a correctness or security bug. Worth a one-line comment in build_conditions noting the interaction is intentional, since it looks surprising next to the AC wording 'querylimit never exceeds max_rows' (that AC is about agent-supplied limit, not operator-supplied forced_conditions).

GoogleGenAIClient.api_key is always None after construction (kwargs.pop before super().__init__ clobber)
payload.body: GoogleGenAIClient.__init__ (client.py:189) does `self.api_key = kwargs.pop('api_key', config.get('GOOGLE_API_KEY'))` BEFORE calling `super().__init__(**kwargs)` (line 196). AbstractClient.__init__ (base.py:448) unconditionally does `self.api_key = kwargs.get('api_key', None)`. Since 'api_key' was already popped out of kwargs by the subclass, the base class always finds it absent and resets self.api_key to None — regardless of whether an explicit api_key kwarg was passed, or GOOGLE_API_KEY resolved from config. GoogleGenAIClient.api_key is ALWAYS None after full construction, independent of caller. Confirmed pre-existing (git blame dates line 189 to commit 0f76129b1, 2026-06-23, months before FEAT-575). Sibling GeminiOpenAICompatClient (openai_compat.py:37) works around the identical hazard by re-setting self.api_key AFTER super().__init__() with an explicit comment referencing this exact clobber pattern (mantle.py:128); GeminiLiveClient (live.py:435) also sets self.api_key after super().__init__(). GoogleGenAIClient never does. Discovered by FEAT-575 TASK-3457's end-to-end integration test (packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/integration/test_crew_google_key_integration.py, both tests currently xfail(strict=True) pending this fix), which is the first test to exercise the full configure()-to-client-construction chain for the 'google' provider with an explicit api_key. Suggested fix: move `self.api_key = kwargs.pop('api_key', config.get('GOOGLE_API_KEY'))` to run AFTER `super().__init__(**kwargs)` in GoogleGenAIClient.__init__, matching the pattern already used in openai_compat.py. Once fixed, remove the two xfail markers in the test file so it will fail loudly if the fix regresses.

payload.title: Review TASK-3457
sdd-coder fidelity gate rejects a task's own correctly-declared sdd/ or gitignore-exception target as 'unexpected_files'
payload.body:
Two confirmed false-positive fidelity_violation outcomes during FEAT-576's implementation, both blocking a coder delivery whose diff exactly matched the task's own Complexity Contract MODIFY targets:

1. TASK-3460 (add taxonomy keys to sdd/templates/{spec,brainstorm,proposal}.md): two independent model attempts (minimax, then native sonnet) each produced a diff touching EXACTLY the 3 declared template files + 1 declared test file — verified byte-for-byte via direct sub-worktree inspection both times — yet coder_merge returned fidelity_violation with unexpected_files listing precisely those 3 template paths. Root cause suspected: sdd/templates/*.md are pre-existing tracked exceptions to the repo's blanket .gitignore 'templates/' rule (documented in this repo's CLAUDE.md 'Heads-up' note); the fidelity gate's declared-vs-actual file comparison appears to mishandle gitignored-but-tracked paths, flagging them as unexpected regardless of git add invocation style.

2. TASK-3468 (add a new section to sdd/WORKFLOW.md — the task's sole, explicitly declared MODIFY target per its own Complexity Contract): a coder attempt (mistral) produced content verified correct (matched byte-for-byte what was ultimately merged) but was rejected with fidelity_violation, unexpected_files: ['sdd/WORKFLOW.md']. This suggests the gate blanket-rejects ANY path under sdd/ regardless of whether the task's own contract declares it as a legitimate target — conflating 'a coder gratuitously touched sdd/tasks/ or sdd/tasks/index/*.json state it was never asked to touch' (the real Cardinal Rule violation this gate should catch) with 'a task's spec-authorized deliverable happens to live under sdd/' (e.g. sdd/WORKFLOW.md, sdd/templates/*.md — both legitimate, human-maintained documentation/template locations, not the per-feature task-state directories the rule is meant to protect).

Impact: both tasks consumed 2 full engine attempts each (4 wasted dispatches, ~15 minutes total, multiple models) before the orchestrator had to self-implement (attempt 3) directly in the main worktree, bypassing the gate entirely — which means the false-positive was never actually diagnosed by the engine itself, just worked around.

Suggested fix: scope the fidelity gate's 'sdd/ is forbidden' rule specifically to sdd/tasks/ (active/completed) and sdd/tasks/index/*.json — the actual per-feature bookkeeping state — rather than the whole sdd/ tree, and audit the declared-vs-actual file comparison for gitignored-but-git-tracked paths (git status/diff already handle this correctly for already-tracked files; whatever the gate uses to enumerate 'expected' files may be filtering through .gitignore incorrectly).

Evidence: FEAT-576 worktree (.claude/worktrees/feat-FEAT-576-sdd-spec-changes), TASK-3460 attempts (minimax attempt_uid 76b3ff8c1e2e47f5898ac29b13fe8dcf, native sonnet attempt_uid ce91b0d3b2a24064a1cacfc9815fa40a) and TASK-3468 attempt (mistral attempt_uid a73a4a0d68464154b175482706db68ad, branch feat-FEAT-576-sdd-spec-changes--TASK-3468-a2-..., commit 59087ea90). Full narrative in each task's Completion Note (sdd/tasks/completed/TASK-3460-templates-taxonomy-keys.md, sdd/tasks/completed/TASK-3468-workflow-docs-taxonomy.md).

payload.title: Redundant frontmatter re-parse in sdd_ingest._process_spec_file and backfill_taxonomy.main
payload.body:
Both call sites independently re-read and re-parse the same document's frontmatter twice: sdd_ingest.py::_process_spec_file calls parse_spec_meta(spec_path) and parse_taxonomy(spec_path) back to back, each doing its own file read + frontmatter split via _read_frontmatter. backfill_taxonomy.py::main() calls plan_edit(doc_path) (which reads+parses internally) and then separately calls infer_projects(original_text) after its own read_text(). Both are batch/offline tooling paths (not hot, not async-critical), so this is a minor inefficiency nitpick, not a defect -- no test or correctness impact. Suggested fix (non-blocking): factor a single read+parse per document and pass the parsed result to both call sites.

payload.title: Crew-level default Google client injection doesn't check credentials_file/credentials/vertexai, only api_key
payload.body: AgentCrew.__init__'s default-Google-orchestration-client injection (crew.py ~line 235-239) only guards with `"api_key" not in kwargs` before adding `api_key=google_api_key`. Unlike the per-agent path (apply_google_api_key, credentials.py, which also checks credentials_file/credentials/vertexai), a caller doing AgentCrew(llm='google', credentials_file=..., google_api_key=X) would get api_key=X injected alongside credentials_file, contradicting docs/crew_handler.md's Precedence section which lists all four as credential signals that should win. Matches the spec's Module 2 interface skeleton literally (FEAT-575 spec section 3), so this may be an accepted spec gap rather than a coding deviation -- needs a product/spec decision on whether to tighten the check to match apply_google_api_key's four-way precedence, or to explicitly scope the docs Precedence section to per-agent injection only. Low real-world exposure today: neither BotManager nor CrewHandler server call site passes credentials_file/vertexai as bare AgentCrew(**kwargs) today. Found during FEAT-575 code review (2026-09-19).

payload.title: sdd-coder lint-autofix bundles whole-file black reformat with functional diffs, inflating reviewable surface
payload.body: TASK-3456's functional change to handler.py was ~10 lines (import + resolve-once + apply-per-agent + AgentCrew kwarg), but the engine's separate 'engine lint autofix' commit (eac25142d) reformatted the entire pre-existing file with black (quote style, multi-line calls collapsed), producing a 231-line diff stat for a 10-line change. A similar dedup of a duplicate 'a' stopword entry occurred in crew.py's TASK-3453 lint-autofix commit (harmless set-literal no-op, confirmed via ruff B033, but still scope creep bundled into a 'style' commit). Not a bug -- no logic changed in either case, spot-checked -- but it inflates the reviewable surface and raises merge-conflict risk against other in-flight work touching the same files (per this repo's documented 'Concurrent SDD sessions hazard'). Suggest scoping the sdd-coder pipeline's autoformatter to touched hunks only, not whole files. Found during FEAT-575 code review (2026-09-19).

payload.title: intake.procedure.md §5f prose disagrees with §6 implementation on collision behavior
payload.body: sdd/templates/intake.procedure.md §5f states: 'No overwrite: If sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/intake/ already exists, abort with an error.' The actual implementation in both .claude/commands/sdd-spec.md and .agent/workflows/sdd-spec.md §6 'Intake mode promotion' does NOT abort — it prints a warning and lets the spec commit proceed, only skipping the promotion step (mirroring the pre-existing design-research promotion pattern at sdd-spec.md ~line 613-624). This may be the intentionally better behavior (never abort the spec commit, consistent with the rest of the feature), but intake.procedure.md is declared the single source of truth for this flow, so its prose should describe what the reference implementation actually does. Found during FEAT-577 adversarial code review. Suggested fix: update §5f prose to match the warn-and-skip behavior, or make the implementation actually abort if that was the real intent — pick one and align both.

payload.title: install_hooks.py render_block bakes an unnormalized repo_root into the shared hook
payload.body: render_block() defaults repo_root to Path.cwd() with no git rev-parse --show-toplevel normalization, baking it into the shared hook's 'cd "{repo_root}"'. Since the hooks dir is shared across all worktrees of a repo, running the installer from inside a linked worktree instead of the primary checkout would bake the wrong path into a hook that fires from the primary checkout — and the failure is swallowed ('>/dev/null 2>&1 || true') with nothing surfaced. Low practical risk (the installer is normally run near repo root) but worth hardening with git rev-parse --show-toplevel. Found during FEAT-577 adversarial code review.

payload.title: install_hooks.py main() uses a broad except Exception around hooks_dir(), masking the real failure reason
payload.body: main() wraps hooks_dir() in a broad 'except Exception:' that silently falls back to repo_root/.git/hooks, masking the specific reason 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks' failed. Should narrow to subprocess.CalledProcessError/OSError so a genuine unexpected error is not swallowed alongside the expected 'not a git repo' case. Found during FEAT-577 adversarial code review.

payload.title: uncaught-exception-on-realistic-input
Non-SDD worktrees never appear in worktree_status --json despite spec resolving to show them
payload.body:
sdd/specs/sdd-status-worktrees.spec.md §8 Open Questions resolved "Should
non-SDD worktrees (chore-*, fix-*) be shown?" as "Yes, in the Worktrees
panel only (no task board entry since they have no per-spec index)."

But discover_worktree_reports() in scripts/sdd/worktree_status.py
unconditionally `continue`s past any branch that doesn't match
_FEAT_BRANCH_RE/_HOTFIX_BRANCH_RE (see the loop body after `_parse_branch`
returns None), so a non-SDD worktree (e.g. chore-ruff-config) never
produces a WorktreeReport entry at all -- --json can never emit it.

.claude/commands/sdd-status.md's new §5 (added by TASK-3551) includes a
worked example showing exactly such a row:

    chore-ruff-config  (non-SDD)
      Branch: chore-ruff-config
      Health: clean

An agent following /sdd-status literally will either hallucinate this row
from nowhere or silently drop the documented behavior, since the data
source the command depends on cannot produce it.

Found by adversarial code review during FEAT-582 (TASK-3549 delivery),
2026-09-19. Not fixed in-feature: AC5 only requires listing "all SDD
worktrees" so this does not fail FEAT-582's own acceptance criteria, and
a proper fix needs a WorktreeReport shape change (feature_slug/feature_id
would need to become fully optional, or a separate lightweight
non-feature entry type) -- bigger than a <5min review-fix.

Suggested fix: either (a) extend WorktreeReport / discover_worktree_reports
to also emit minimal entries for parsed-but-unmatched branches (no tasks,
no ready_for_done), or (b) remove the worked example from
.claude/commands/sdd-status.md §5 and .agents/skills/sdd-status/SKILL.md
step 6 to match actual behavior.

payload.title: _check_health ignores git returncode, so a failed check reads as 'clean'
payload.body:
scripts/sdd/worktree_status.py:_check_health calls _git("status",
"--porcelain", ...) and _git("log", f"origin/{base_branch}..HEAD", ...)
but never checks .returncode on either result. If origin/<base_branch>
doesn't exist locally (stale/unfetched remote-tracking ref -- plausible
for a worktree branched from `staging` during a release freeze, or simply
not fetched recently) or git errors for any other reason, stdout is empty
and the code silently reports unpushed_count=0 / dirty_count=0 -- i.e.
"clean". Since AC7's ready_for_done gate exists specifically to avoid
unsafe /sdd-done suggestions, treating "couldn't check" the same as
"confirmed clean" is a real risk, not cosmetic.

Found by adversarial code review during FEAT-582 (TASK-3549), 2026-09-19.
Deferred as a SUGGESTION (not blocking FEAT-582's own AC7, which only
requires the happy-path semantics); worth an "unknown" health state in a
follow-up.

payload.title: discover_worktree_reports output order is nondeterministic (set-based)
payload.body:
all_worktree_paths in discover_worktree_reports() is a set(), so both the
--json array order and the plain-table row order vary across runs with
the same underlying git/filesystem state. For a status/observability tool
people will screen-diff run to run, this is friction. Suggested fix: sort
reports by branch (or feature_slug) before returning.

Found by adversarial code review during FEAT-582 (TASK-3549), 2026-09-19.
Deferred as a SUGGESTION -- does not affect AC2/AC3 correctness.

payload.title: _read_worktree_index's except clause doesn't cover all realistic OSError subtypes
payload.body:
_read_worktree_index's outer `except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError,
KeyError):` doesn't cover PermissionError / IsADirectoryError /
UnicodeDecodeError, all of which open()/json.load() can raise for a
plausible worktree index file. Consider broadening to OSError in addition
to the JSON/KeyError cases, for the same "never crash the whole scan over
one bad worktree" reasoning that motivated the two CRITICAL fixes already
applied in this feature (fix commit 2c3efff45).

Found by adversarial code review during FEAT-582 (TASK-3549), 2026-09-19.
Deferred as a SUGGESTION -- no reproduction of an actual crash from these
specific subtypes, unlike the two CRITICAL cases that were fixed.

payload.title: worktree_status CLI table prints feature_id twice (Name column + Feature column)
payload.body:
main()'s plain-table printer folds feature_id into the "Name" column
(f"{slug} ({feature_id})") and also prints it again in the dedicated
"Feature" column. Not incorrect (AC3's required columns are all present),
just redundant/cosmetic.

Found by adversarial code review during FEAT-582 (TASK-3549), 2026-09-19.
Deferred as a NITPICK.

payload.title: Misleading anchor comment for WORKTREE_ROOT import (line 15 is a re-export, not the definition)
payload.body:
scripts/sdd/worktree_status.py's import comment
`from scripts.sdd.sdd_meta import WORKTREE_ROOT  # verified:
scripts/sdd/sdd_meta.py:15` is technically true (that's where the name
appears in an import list) but the actual WORKTREE_ROOT *definition* is
in packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/ledger/sdd_meta.py:322.
The comment could mislead a future reader into thinking line 15 is the
definition rather than a re-export.

Found by adversarial code review during FEAT-582 (TASK-3549), 2026-09-19.
Deferred as a NITPICK.

payload.title: Review TASK-3510
parrot-sdd-coder: no eligible seat (MCP or native) for 'unknown' complexity classification
payload.body: TASK-3508 and TASK-3511 (FEAT-580) were both assessed classification=unknown (reason_code=metric_unknown, wiki blast-radius collector exit 1 for their contract symbols). Every MCP seat probed across all three backends -- nova (glm, minimax, qwen, mistral), google-compat (gemini), codex (codex-spark) -- was rejected at dispatch time with 'CoderFailure: seat ... is not eligible for unknown task <id>'. coder_prepare_native also refused with task_not_in_plan since the planner never routes 'unknown' classification to a native seat either. Net effect: an 'unknown'-classified task can never be dispatched by any seat kind under the current routing policy, permanently blocking it and its transitive dependents. Reproduced identically across 3 separate coder_plan/coder_run_chunk cycles (6 distinct MCP seats, 0 successes). Fix: either add 'unknown' classification to the eligible-seat allowlist for at least one backend (e.g. treat it like 'complex', restricted to strong-model seats), or make coder_plan itself refuse to assign an mcp seat_label for a classification it knows no seat accepts, surfacing a routing_block instead of a doomed dispatch.

payload.title: LSPToolkit never calls self.logger (0 log lines in a 938-line stateful component)
payload.body: No log on session restart, close, idle shutdown, or any LSPFailure->LSPResult conversion. CLAUDE.md mandates self.logger over silence; PyrightSession and _ToolkitStdioMCPServer both log correctly, LSPToolkit is the outlier. Add debug-level logs on start/restart/close and warning-level on failures. Found in FEAT-580 code review (adversarial review of TASK-3499-3510).

payload.title: PyrightSession never cross-checks initialize's serverInfo.version
payload.body: Spec sec2 point 6 requires comparing any supplied serverInfo.version too. _handshake() (session.py) only reads capabilities from the initialize response, discarding serverInfo entirely (confirmed: zero matches for 'serverInfo' in lsp/). A server_command pointing at a different Pyright build than the independently-invoked version_command reports goes undetected. Found in FEAT-580 code review (adversarial review of TASK-3499-3510).

payload.title: Diagnostic baseline tests miss line-shift dedup and 2 of 3 baseline_incompatible branches
payload.body: Every diagnostic fixture in test_diagnostic_baselines.py uses line=1, so no test proves two diagnostics differing only by line/range are correctly treated as the same diagnostic (the behavior _diagnostic_key in toolkit.py is designed for). Separately, baseline_incompatible() (toolkit.py) is an OR of environment_id/server_version/config_digest mismatches; only the environment_id branch has a test (test_incompatible_identity_is_rejected_explicitly). Add tests for line-shifted-but-otherwise-identical diagnostics staying deduped, and for the server_version and config_digest incompatibility branches. Found in FEAT-580 code review (adversarial review of TASK-3499-3510).

payload.title: _reader_loop doesn't wake blocked diagnostic waiters on server crash
payload.body: _reader_loop sets self._crashed = True on a protocol failure but never signals self._notification_event, so an in-flight diagnostics() call won't observe the crash until its full diagnostics_timeout_s elapses instead of failing fast. Eventual correctness is preserved, just slower than necessary. Found in FEAT-580 code review (adversarial review of TASK-3499-3510).

payload.title: _is_manifest_relevant doesn't follow pyrightconfig.json's extends chain
payload.body: Spec sec2.3 says referenced in-root Pyright configuration files are part of the digest; the implementation only matches a fixed basename set, so an extends-based config layering wouldn't correctly invalidate the session on a referenced-file change. Narrow gap, worth a follow-up before the M6 live run. Found in FEAT-580 code review (adversarial review of TASK-3499-3510).

payload.title: Shutdown timeouts default to 5.0s, not spec-pinned 2s; version parsing takes first version-shaped substring
payload.body: Two small deviations found in FEAT-580 code review: (1) shutdown_timeout_s/terminate_timeout_s/kill_timeout_s all default 5.0s, deviating from spec sec2 point 11's literal 'waits 2 seconds' pinned values (more lenient, not less, but undocumented) and aren't in the spec's list of configurable fields; (2) version-string parsing (session.py, re.search(r'\d+\.\d+\.\d+', output)) takes the first version-shaped substring anywhere in pyright --version output, which would misattribute if a wrapper prints something else version-shaped first (e.g. a Node banner).

payload.title: ESCALATE: _terminate_process signals only the immediate child PID, not a process group
payload.body: _terminate_process (session.py) signals only the immediate child PID -- if pyright-langserver spawns Node worker/watcher subprocesses, they would not receive terminate()/kill(). Unverified in this environment: no real Pyright 1.1.414 binary provisioned to confirm against the actual process topology. Flagged as ESCALATE (not CONFIRM) in FEAT-580's adversarial code review -- needs checking once the pinned integration tests run for real against a provisioned Pyright (M6 live run).

payload.title: run_behavior_check uses blocking subprocess.run -- must not be called from async runner.py
payload.body: benchmarks/sdd_lsp/fixtures/acceptance.py::run_behavior_check uses blocking subprocess.run. Harmless today since no async caller exists yet, but the eventual runner.py (TASK-3511, currently blocked on FEAT-580's routing-engine gap -- see issue:f0cf45fc31dd) must not call this from 'async def run_pilot' without moving to asyncio.create_subprocess_exec or asyncio.to_thread. Forward-looking note from FEAT-580's adversarial code review, not a current bug.

payload.title: _relative_to_root/_uri_for_path build/compare paths slightly asymmetrically
payload.body: toolkit.py's _relative_to_root/_uri_for_path build/compare an unresolved 'repo_root / path' against a resolved _canonical_root -- likely fine if LSPConfig canonicalizes repo_root, but worth a one-line confirmation. Found in FEAT-580 code review (adversarial review of TASK-3499-3510).

payload.title: LSPFailure silently truncates detail to 1000 chars, inconsistent with explicit-truncation philosophy
payload.body: LSPFailure.__init__ (models.py) truncates detail to 1000 chars silently, inconsistent with the module's 'truncation must be explicit' philosophy elsewhere. Nitpick from FEAT-580's adversarial code review.

payload.title: Confirm 'result_limit' operational error code from spec's Data Models table is not dead
payload.body: 'result_limit' is a named operational error code in the spec's Data Models table but doesn't appear to be referenced in toolkit.py's merged code. Worth a one-line confirmation it belongs to a manifest-size case elsewhere, or is currently dead. Nitpick from FEAT-580's adversarial code review.

run_pilot never populates AttemptRecord.tool_calls/lsp_operations/correction_cycles/retries
payload.body: TASK-3511's own acceptance criteria say to collect retries, resource/cold-warm metrics alongside acceptance/failure -- but _run_one_attempt's AttemptRecord(...) construction (runner.py) never sets tool_calls, lsp_operations, correction_cycles, or retries; they silently default to 0 for every real attempt. report.py's per-arm correction_cycles_total/retries_total will always read 0 in a real run. Fix direction: the seat protocol needs a way to report these (e.g. additional fields in trace.jsonl's per-attempt summary, or a separate attempt_meta.json), then thread them into AttemptRecord. Confirmed by independent adversarial review (two reviewers) during FEAT-580 TASK-3511/3512 review-fix round.

payload.title: Review TASK-3532
sdd-coder run_chunk: job runner scheduled before background handle registration (handle may stay `running`)
payload.body:
In `SddCoderEngine.run_chunk` (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/flows/dev_loop/sdd_coder/engine.py, the `job = self._jobs.create(...)` call followed by the `if self._background_registry is not None and execution_id:` block), `JobTable.create()` schedules the runner coroutine immediately. Registration of the FEAT-584 M8 background handle then awaits two disk writes (`register()` + `_record_transition(state="running")`) before `self._handle_execution[job.job_id]` is populated.

The runner's terminal settlement is guarded by `if job.job_id in self._handle_execution:`. A runner that finishes before registration completes (e.g. every task fails immediately at dispatch) evaluates that guard as False and skips `_record_transition(state="finished", ...)`. Registration then lands afterwards and leaves the durable handle in `running` forever although the job is done; `coder_bg_status` and the `end_execution`/`cleanup` settlement gates read stale state.

Pre-existing on telemetry-enabled engines (`telemetry_dir` / `DEV_LOOP_CODER_TELEMETRY=true`). Exposed to every default install by the fix that binds the evidence store (and therefore `BackgroundRegistry`) unconditionally (branch fix-sdd-coder-evidence-store-always-on, 2026-09-21). Fix direction: complete registration (and the `_handle_execution` bookkeeping) BEFORE the runner may execute — e.g. register first and only then create/schedule the job, or have `JobTable.create` accept a deferred start. Add a regression test with a runner that completes synchronously.

Found by the codex adversarial review of that branch; verified by reading the code, not reproduced at runtime.

payload.title: Review TASK-3583
end_execution's outstanding_job_ids never filters by completion state, permanently poisoning the settlement snapshot and blocking review_checkpoint prepare
payload.body: SddCoderEngine._job_worktrees (engine.py:382) records job_id -> worktree at dispatch (engine.py:3510, inside run_chunk) and is NEVER removed anywhere in the file (grep -n '_job_worktrees' finds only the declaration, the two enrichment loops, and the dispatch-time write -- no del/pop). end_execution's snapshot enrichment (engine.py:812-815) unconditionally copies EVERY entry whose worktree matches into snapshot.outstanding_job_ids, with no check on the job's actual state (done/running/failed) via self._jobs or self._background_registry. The identical unconditional-copy bug is repeated in the persistence-degraded recovery path (engine.py:2562-2564). Confirmed reproduced on FEAT-588: after coder_end_execution succeeded (returned status=closed, no complaint -- because pool status was already naturally closed, bypassing the busy checks at engine.py:772-796 that are gated behind 'if view.status != closed'), python -m scripts.sdd.review_checkpoint prepare then failed with checkpoint_busy: 'settlement for execution ... still lists outstanding work: 0 attempt(s), 0 reservation(s), 2 job(s)' even though both job-b9696e396e71 and job-4a0981277800 were independently confirmed state=done with outcome=merged via coder_status. This means review_checkpoint prepare (FEAT-584 M4/R5, the mandatory gate before the adversarial code-reviewer per sdd-worker's Completion section) can NEVER succeed for any execution that dispatched at least one coder_run_chunk job, which is virtually every real sdd-worker session -- a systemic, not edge-case, defect. Suggested fix: before appending to outstanding_job_ids in both loops, check the job's actual terminal state (e.g. via self._jobs.get(job_id).state or self._background_registry) and skip/remove entries that are already done/finished; alternatively pop from self._job_worktrees once a job reaches a terminal state in wait()/status().

payload.title: Vacuous-truth edge case in the MCP-only retry-ladder diagnostic (all() over an empty generator)
payload.body: In the new 'MCP-only retry ladder' diagnostic branch (engine.py ~3315-3323, added by FEAT-588), the expression all(candidate.kind == "native" for candidate in pool._seats if candidate.label in remaining) is vacuously True when no seat in pool._seats matches any label in remaining (empty generator). In practice remaining is always derived from the same roster's seats so this is low risk today, but it should be hardened: compute remaining_seats = [...] first and guard with 'if remaining_seats and all(...)' to remove the vacuous-truth possibility before it can silently mis-diagnose a future roster shape.

payload.title: Undocumented design choice: native retry handoff has no busy-wait, unlike the MCP retry selector
payload.body: _select_native_retry_seat (engine.py, added by FEAT-588) does a single pass with no busy-wait, unlike _select_retry_seat which loops on pool._condition.wait() for a busy-but-healthy MCP seat. Net effect: a busy MCP seat is waited on and preferred over an idle native seat, and a busy native seat is never waited for — it falls through to the blocked diagnostic instead. Exercised by the existing busy-native-seat test and looks intentional (MCP preferred; native handoff is a last resort, not a queued reservation), but this design decision is not called out anywhere in comments or docs. Add a one-line comment/docstring note explaining the intentional asymmetry.

payload.body: FEAT-588 added the native retry handoff only on the pool-based path (AC-9/NG2). Local-scenario status not downgraded for per-case-only failures
payload.body: artifacts/laya/evaluate.py:160-161 only flips top-level EvaluationReport.status away from 'complete' when a sample's error_code is 'inference_timeout' or 'worker_failed'. Other per-case codes (context_overflow, invalid_answer) never flip status, so a scenario where 100% of cases fail for a per-case reason can still report top-level status='complete' (visible only via errors_by_code, not the exit code). Found during FEAT-589 code review. Suggested fix: flip to incomplete when n_error == n_cases for any scenario, or document the nuance in the README.

payload.body: artifacts/laya/runtime.py:204-223 (_shutdown) — if proc.wait() still times out after proc.kill(), the loop exhausts silently and self._proc = None is set regardless of whether the OS process actually exited. AgentsFlow definition-driven scheduler never fires the required checkpoint barrier, so plan_resume always re-dispatches completed nodes
payload.body: AgentsFlow._run_flow_scheduler()'s 'required checkpoint barrier' (_await_required_barrier(), flow.py lines ~2293-2321) is only invoked inside the 'if explicit_mode:' branch, where explicit_mode = self._definition is None and bool(self._edges). PlanFlow (tools/execution_plan/checkpoint.py) is built via PlanFlow.from_definition(), which sets self._definition to a non-None FlowDefinition -- so explicit_mode is always False for any plan-based flow, and the incremental per-node-completion checkpoint write NEVER fires. Only the start ('running') and terminal checkpoints get written (PlanFlow._run_flow_scheduler wraps super()._run_flow_scheduler with those two writes only). Confirmed via direct reproduction (FEAT-585 TASK-3600 consolidation, 2026-09-22): after running a 3-node sequential plan (a->b->c) with checkpoint=True and cancelling mid-flight at node c, the persisted checkpoint has put_calls=1 and node_states=[] -- i.e. a and b's completions were never persisted. Calling plan_resume() therefore rebuilds the flow with zero completed-node state and re-dispatches every node from scratch, defeating the entire point of checkpointed resume. This blocks FEAT-585 TASK-3600's own AC ('no re-dispatch of completed nodes on resume', see packages/ai-parrot/tests/tools/execution_plan/test_checkpoint_resume.py::test_resume_does_not_redispatch_completed_and_completes_rest, currently failing: dispatch_counts={'a':2,'b':2,'c':2} instead of the expected {'a':1,'b':1,'c':2}) and will very likely also block TASK-3601 (plan_repair) and TASK-3602 (integration recovery tests), both of which depend directly on TASK-3600 and the same PlanFlow/checkpoint machinery. Suggested fix: either (a) make the required-barrier persistence unconditional on explicit_mode (persist after every node completion regardless of scheduler mode), or (b) build PlanFlow via the explicit add_node()/add_edge() path instead of from_definition() -- but per flow.py's own resume() docstring, from_definition() was deliberately chosen for plan flows to preserve predicate/back-edge semantics that the explicit-edge path implements differently, so (a) is likely the safer fix. Either way this touches core AgentsFlow scheduler code (flow.py) used far beyond plan execution, well outside any single FEAT-585 task's file scope -- needs its own task/spec amendment, not a same-task patch.

payload.title: PlanContinuation's stale-snapshot check compares a resolved child's checkpoint_id against the ROOT's own sequence, always misfiring once a lineage has an accepted child
payload.body: PlanRunResolver.resolve() (runs.py ~290-326) walks a run's lineage into its active_child_run_id when one exists, and returns the CHILD's own checkpoint_id in the resulting PlanRun.checkpoint_id (runs.py:322-326: 'current_checkpoint, current_metadata = child_checkpoint, child_metadata' then 'checkpoint_id=current_checkpoint.checkpoint_id'). PlanContinuation.__aenter__ (checkpoint.py ~216-230) then does: 'self._root = run.metadata.root_run_id' (correctly the ROOT id) but its staleness check is 'latest = await select_latest(self._store, self._durable, self._root); if latest is None or latest.checkpoint_id != self._run.checkpoint_id: raise PlanRunError("run_busy", "stale snapshot: re-resolve the run")' -- select_latest reads the checkpoint for flow_id=self._root (the ROOT's OWN independently-numbered checkpoint sequence), while self._run.checkpoint_id (when the resolved run descended into a child) is the CHILD's own independently-numbered checkpoint_id under a DIFFERENT flow_id. These two ids belong to unrelated monotonic sequences and will essentially never coincidentally match, so this check incorrectly raises 'run_busy' ('stale snapshot') on every single-process, uncontended plan_resume/plan_repair call made against a run whose current resolved view has already descended into an accepted child -- e.g. resuming an interrupted repair child, or attempting a second plan_repair on a lineage with one already-accepted child. Confirmed via direct reproduction (FEAT-585 TASK-3603, 2026-09-22): packages/ai-parrot/tests/tools/execution_plan/test_integration_repair.py::test_crash_p3_after_child_accepted calls plan_resume on exactly such a run and gets 'run_busy' every time, with zero contention (single process, no other continuation ever held the lease). This is DISTINCT from ledger issue:7552079c55a1 (which blocks resuming mid-child-execution with no incremental checkpoint at all) -- this defect blocks even the P3 case where the child DOES have a valid checkpoint to resume from. Neither TASK-3600's nor TASK-3601's own test suites exercise 'call plan_resume/plan_repair again on a lineage that already has an accepted child with its own checkpoint', so this was never previously exercised. Likely fix: PlanContinuation's staleness check should validate against the checkpoint_id of the ROOT's own latest checkpoint as originally resolved (before any lineage descent), not against whatever leaf checkpoint_id the fully-descended PlanRun view carries -- the resolver may need to separately expose the root's own checkpoint_id alongside the leaf's for this comparison, or PlanContinuation should re-derive it from run.metadata.root_run_id via its own root-scoped resolve rather than trusting run.checkpoint_id directly.

payload.title: Migrate Telegram voice replies from GoogleTTSBackend to Supertonic TTS
payload.body:
Follow-up to the speech-report-models brainstorm (sdd/proposals/speech-report-models.brainstorm.md, commit 05259778e).

WHY: that feature changes GoogleTTSBackend to wrap its raw Gemini PCM in a WAV header and report the truthful mime_format (audio/wav). Today Telegram voice replies (FEAT-213) consume GoogleTTSBackend output as raw PCM. Rather than adapt Telegram to the new Google output, migrate it to Supertonic, which is faster (local ONNX, sub-second) and free.

SCOPE:
- TelegramAgentConfig.tts_backend default "google" -> "supertonic" (packages/ai-parrot-integrations/src/parrot/integrations/telegram/models.py:142 and the from-dict default at :303). Keep "google" selectable.
- TelegramAgentWrapper._get_synthesizer (wrapper.py:3204) builds a TTSConfig(backend=self.config.tts_backend, ...). Pass the Supertonic knobs (speed, total_step) through if they are exposed in the config.
- Voice ids differ by backend: Google uses Charon/Kore, Supertonic uses M1..F5. Map or validate tts_voice per backend so a leftover Google voice id does not break Supertonic.

- Reuse the process-wide synthesizer cache introduced by speech-report-models so the ONNX model loads once per process across the Telegram wrapper and agents.
- Update tests: packages/ai-parrot-integrations/tests/test_telegram_voice_reply.py and tests/voice/tts/test_tts_integration.py.

payload.title: Review TASK-3638
review_checkpoint prepare: stale outstanding_job_ids blocks settlement despite coder_end_execution reporting closed
payload.body:
FEAT-590 orchestrator run, execution_id 6f9e6a1e-3f4a-4b6a-9c5d-1e2f3a4b5c6d.
coder_end_execution returned status="closed" with 0 admitted attempts/native
reservations. coder_plan immediately after showed pending=[] blocked=[]
next_chunk=null (all 15 tasks done). coder_cleanup removed all 15 sub-
worktrees with kept=[]. Every coder_run_chunk job across the run (7 distinct
job ids) was individually confirmed state="done" via coder_wait before
moving on.

Despite this, `python -m scripts.sdd.review_checkpoint prepare` refuses with
checkpoint_busy: "0 attempt(s), 0 reservation(s), 8 job(s)" -- the durable
ExecutionSnapshot's outstanding_job_ids still lists 8 entries even though
coder_end_execution already published a "closed" settlement and every job
was independently verified done. This means prepare_review_checkpoint
(checkpoint.py) and coder_end_execution disagree about job settlement,
blocking the review-checkpoint step for any execution that ran the normal
number of chunked waves (this run had 7-8 coder_run_chunk calls, not an
edge case).

Suggested fix: audit whether coder_run_chunk/coder_wait job completion is
supposed to clear the job id from the same outstanding-jobs ledger that
coder_end_execution reads before publishing "closed", or whether
coder_end_execution's own closed-ness check is insufficiently strict (i.e.
it should have refused to close if jobs were truly outstanding).

Workaround used here: treated this as a checkpoint-tooling bug (verified
independently via coder_plan/coder_cleanup that no real work was
outstanding), noted as "checkpoint: unavailable (stale settlement)" in the
completion summary, and proceeded straight to code review on the settled
worktree state -- same posture as the documented no-engine/unsupported-host
fallback.

payload.title: test_fresh_process_recovery_chain fails on a clean dev checkout
payload.body: Discovered during FEAT-590 code review, but confirmed pre-existing and unrelated: the test file is byte-identical to origin/dev (git diff origin/dev -- <file> is empty), and it reproduces identically (Node 'c' failed: "'b_out' not found. Available: []") in a throwaway origin/dev worktree with its compiled .so extensions copied in (independently verified myself, not just taking a reviewer's word for it). Likely a checkpoint/artifact-resolution ordering bug in the recovery-chain path (parrot/tools/execution_plan/checkpoint.py or toolkit.py) surfaced by this test's own fresh-process simulation. Suggested fix: bisect the recovery-chain resume path for why node 'c' cannot see node 'b's stored artifact ('b_out') after a simulated process restart.

payload.title: NeedleDelegate proposals always report latency_ms=0.0
payload.body: needle.py's propose_call() builds every ToolCallProposal with latency_ms=0.0 and a comment 'Will be set by the caller' -- but delegate/node.py's _propose_with_chain() never patches it after awaiting delegate.propose_call() (confirmed by reading the call site directly: no latency_ms assignment anywhere near line ~123). Contrast with llamacpp.py's propose_call(), which measures started=time.monotonic() itself and returns a real latency_ms. Every Needle-backend DelegateTrace/proposal therefore reports 0.0 latency, which is a real (if minor) observability gap, not a hypothetical one. Fix: either measure latency inside NeedleDelegate.propose_call() itself (matching llamacpp.py's pattern), or have _propose_with_chain() time the propose_call() await and overwrite proposal.latency_ms before tracing.

payload.title: Duplicated AbstractTool-vs-ToolDefinition hasattr branching
payload.body: protocol.py's tool_specs() and node.py's _gate() both independently branch on hasattr(tool, 'get_schema') vs tool.input_schema to distinguish AbstractTool from ToolDefinition (confirmed by reading both sites). Candidate for a small shared helper (e.g. a get_tool_parameters(tool) function) so the two call sites cannot silently drift. Not fixed here: out of FEAT-590's task scope, code-review suggestion only.

payload.title: repair.py can emit both delta_protected_id and delta_delegate_not_repairable for one node
payload.body: validate_delta()'s delta_protected_id check (~lines 127-134) does not continue before the delegate check (~lines 136-144) runs, so a delegate node that is ALSO protected produces two issues in one PlanDelta validation report instead of one. Confirmed by reading the two checks directly. The reviewer judged this harmless today, but flagged it is unconfirmed whether any downstream consumer assumes exactly one issue per node -- worth a quick audit before relying on that assumption. Not fixed here: speculative-severity code-review suggestion, out of FEAT-590's task scope.

SddCoderEngine._job_worktrees is never cleared, so MCP run_chunk deliveries can never reach a review checkpoint
payload.body: SddCoderEngine._job_worktrees is populated in run_chunk (engine.py, `self._job_worktrees[job.job_id] = ctx.worktree`) and never removed anywhere in engine.py (no pop/del). end_execution unconditionally appends every job id ever dispatched for the worktree to ExecutionSnapshot.outstanding_job_ids without checking the job's terminal state, and prepare_review_checkpoint (checkpoint.py) treats any non-empty outstanding_job_ids as still busy. Result: a real MCP delivery via run_chunk can never reach a valid review checkpoint, even long after the job is done/merged; there is no public API to clear the entry. test_optimization_workflow_contracts.py works around it with an explicit commented test-only reset. Suggested fix: drop the job from _job_worktrees when it reaches a terminal state (merge/cleanup/wait terminal), and in end_execution only report jobs whose status is non-terminal; then remove the test workaround. Found by the TASK-3575 coder (FEAT-584); originally NOT filed because the shared ledger was read-only in the sandbox.

This matches a previously-noted open gap ("empty-diff-passes-fidelity gap still open", tracked alongside PR #1460 which fixed gitignored declared files + ledger retract-feedback for a related class of extraction bugs). Likely root cause per that same context: codex seats cannot commit themselves — the engine extracts and commits their patch on their behalf — so an extraction failure here silently produces a no-op merge that the fidelity gate does not distinguish from "task genuinely required no changes."

Suggested fix: the merge/fidelity gate should treat commits=0 (or changed_files=[]) against a task with a non-empty declared CREATE/MODIFY file contract as a hard failure, not a pass — never as "merged".

payload.title: Review TASK-3536
sdd/state/e2e/ not gitignored — leaves untracked cruft after any e2e test run
payload.body:
Running any test under packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/e2e/ (or the unit/e2e real-subprocess tests) against a real worktree writes persisted RunState/evidence under sdd/state/e2e/. Unlike sdd/state/.design_research/, this path is not in .gitignore, so it shows up as untracked cruft in git status after any e2e run.

Discovered while implementing TASK-3537 (FEAT-581) — not introduced by that task, pre-existing since TASK-3524's e2e-run-state work. Suggested fix: add sdd/state/e2e/ (or a narrower per-run-id pattern) to .gitignore.

payload.title: packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/unit/e2e/ real-subprocess tests are flaky when run together (resource contention, not code bugs)
payload.body:
Running the full packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/unit/e2e/ directory together produces ~18 intermittent failures across test_supervisor.py, test_watchdog.py, test_ui_browser_targets.py, test_state.py, test_mcp_targets.py and test_crash_probe_contract.py — real-subprocess-spawning tests that all pass cleanly (19/19, 5/5, etc.) when run individually or file-by-file. The specific set of failing tests varies between runs (confirmed via two consecutive full-suite runs producing different failure sets), consistent with resource contention (process/fd/port limits) under this sandboxed environment when many real subprocess tests run back-to-back, not a code regression.

Discovered while verifying TASK-3537 (FEAT-581): its own declared file (test_crash_probe_contract.py) passes standalone (5/5); the pre-existing test_supervisor.py (untouched by TASK-3537) passes 19/19 alone but fails intermittently only as part of the full sweep.

Suggested fix: either serialize/isolate real-subprocess e2e unit tests (e.g. pytest-xdist worker pinning, or a session-scoped semaphore), or raise the sandbox's process/fd ulimits for this test tier, or explicitly document that this test directory must be run per-file rather than as a whole sweep in constrained environments.

payload.title: Review TASK-3537
E2E runner bridge node-ID lookup breaks for nested-package test paths (false FAIL on full plan run)
payload.body:
`_bridge_results()` in `packages/ai-parrot-server/src/parrot/e2e/runner.py` (~line 273-283) looks up `observed.get(node_id)` using `scenario.node_ids`, which are repo-root-relative per the E2E plan schema (e.g. `packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/e2e/test_mcp_http.py::test_http_cli_stays_alive_and_stops`). But the actual pytest subprocess is invoked with `packages/ai-parrot-server` as rootdir (its own `pyproject.toml`), so the persisted bridge JSON records the SAME test under a package-relative key (`tests/e2e/test_mcp_http.py::...`, no `packages/ai-parrot-server/` prefix). The `observed.get(node_id)` lookup therefore never matches, even though the test genuinely ran and passed — `_bridge_results` falls through to the "missing"/`node_not_collected` branch (line 283) for every scenario, producing an aggregate verdict of `FAIL`/`gate_satisfied: false` even when every individual scenario's pytest invocation passed.

Verified directly during TASK-3547 (FEAT-581) work: ran `PARROT_TEST_E2E=1 parrot e2e run --plan sdd/state/FEAT-581/e2e-plan.md` for real; every one of the 7 non-redis scenarios' pytest subprocess reported "1 passed" in the raw streamed output and in the raw bridge JSON file on disk (under the unprefixed spelling), but the persisted `e2e-verdict.json` marked all 7 as `outcome: "missing"`, `reason_code: "node_not_collected"`, with overall `status: FAIL`, `exit_code: 4`.

This blocks a genuine full-plan PASS today and undermines AC17 (deterministic plan actually gates/gates correctly) even though the underlying test coverage is real and green. Suggested fix: normalize both sides (plan node_ids and bridge-observed keys) to the same relative base before the `observed.get(node_id)` lookup — either always repo-root-relative or always rootdir-relative, applied consistently in both `runner.py`'s scenario selection and whatever writes the bridge JSON.

Not fixed in TASK-3547 because `runner.py`/`evidence.py` are outside that task's declared file scope (packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/e2e/test_evidence.py, sdd/state/FEAT-581/e2e-plan.md, sdd/specs/agentic-e2e-testing.spec.md, tests/sdd_scripts/test_feat581_plan.py only).

payload.title: test_target_registry.py assumes mcp-agent target is still unimplemented (stale since TASK-3540)
payload.body:
`packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/unit/e2e/test_target_registry.py::test_get_target_adapter_raises_prerequisite_error_for_unimplemented_kind[mcp-agent]` and `::test_get_target_adapter_only_imports_the_requested_module` both use `"mcp-agent"` as the "still-genuinely-unimplemented kind" fixture case. TASK-3540 (FEAT-581) landed a real `mcp-agent` target adapter in `parrot/e2e/targets/mcp.py` (`build_mcp_agent_adapter`), so `get_target_adapter("mcp-agent")` no longer raises `E2EPrerequisiteError` — both tests now fail with "DID NOT RAISE E2EPrerequisiteError". The second test's own docstring already flags this exact pattern happening once before for "browser" (fixed by switching the fixture kind), but wasn't updated when `mcp-agent` landed too.

Fix: pick a genuinely-still-unimplemented target kind for both fixtures (check `parrot.e2e.targets`'s registry for one), or restructure the tests to use a synthetic/fake unregistered kind instead of a real one that may land during the same feature.

Reproduced independently of the FEAT-581 review-fix commit (confirmed via `git stash`) — pre-existing, not introduced by the two critical-finding fixes (evidence.py exclusion gap, runner.py node-ID bridge mismatch) made during FEAT-581 completion.

payload.title: AC9 closeout enforcement (E2E gate blocks /sdd-done on BLOCKED/FAIL) is prompt-only, not code-enforced
payload.body:
FEAT-581 AC9 states "Claude/Codex closeout checks the same evidence contract before mutations; generic force cannot bypass required E2E." The actual enforcement lives entirely in markdown instructions (.claude/commands/sdd-done.md Step 4.6, .agents/skills/sdd-done/SKILL.md Step 4.5) telling the executing agent to abort — not in a code invariant. `verify_evidence` itself is sound and takes no `force` argument, but nothing structurally prevents an executing agent from ignoring/misreading those instructions and proceeding anyway.

`tests/sdd_scripts/test_e2e_closeout_contract.py`'s own `evaluate_closeout_gate()` is an explicitly-labeled test-only reimplementation of the documented decision table, proven against the real `verify_evidence` validator — it does not (and structurally cannot, since the production flow is agent-interpreted prose) exercise the real sdd-done.md command end-to-end.

Contrast: the dev-loop's own QA node (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/flows/dev_loop/nodes/qa.py:361-364) ANDs the E2E gate into `passed` in real Python — AC10 is solidly code-enforced; AC9 for the Claude/Codex closeout surface specifically is not, despite the AC's wording.

This mirrors the pre-existing architecture of every other /sdd-done gate (not a regression FEAT-581 introduces), so not a blocker, but the acceptance-criterion language overstates what's structurally guaranteed. Consider either softening AC9's wording to reflect prompt-level enforcement, or (bigger lift) adding a real code-level check /sdd-done invokes before any push/merge, similar to qa.py's pattern.

Found during FEAT-581 (TASK-3543) code review.

payload.title: Exploration subagents (e2e-api-tester/e2e-ui-tester) have unscoped Write tool grant
payload.body:
.claude/agents/e2e-api-tester.md and e2e-ui-tester.md declare `tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep, Write` with no path restriction. AC12 requires "candidate tests are outside discovery and promotion requires human review" — nothing technically stops either agent from writing a candidate test directly into `tests/` against its own prompt instructions; "human-only promotion" is enforced by prompt discipline only, not a hard control.

Mitigated in practice: the deterministic gate only ever reads plan-declared node IDs (evidence.py has zero references to exploration output paths, and ScenarioSpec validators reject tier=exploratory + required=true), so even a rogue write couldn't flip a gate result without a separate human edit to the plan. Still worth tightening the tool grant (e.g. restrict Write to the exploration output directory only) for defense-in-depth.

Found during FEAT-581 (TASK-3544) code review.

payload.title: CLI `up`'s "survives launcher exit" claim (AC5) has no real-subprocess integration test
payload.body:
The `up` command's detached-daemon lifecycle (packages/ai-parrot-server/src/parrot/e2e/cli.py, `_run_daemon`/`_spawn_detached_target`) is unit-tested only with monkeypatched `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` and a faked `E2ESupervisor` (test_cli.py:302-419). The design is plausible (`start_new_session=True`), but there is no integration test that actually spawns `up`, kills the invoking CLI process, and confirms the daemon+target genuinely survive — the specific sub-claim of AC5 ("survives launcher exit") is designed-for, not empirically verified.

This belongs to a real-subprocess acceptance-test tier (per TASK-3534's own note: "the real-subprocess acceptance-test tier for this lifecycle belongs to the M5/M9 integration/E2E scenario suite, not this task's tests/unit/e2e/test_cli.py"), which was never built as a dedicated task.

Found during FEAT-581 (TASK-3534) code review.

payload.title: e2e.yml uses if-no-files-found: warn on failure-artifact upload (AC14 weakens silent-gap trail)
payload.body:
.github/workflows/e2e.yml uses `if-no-files-found: warn` on both `upload-artifact` steps (deterministic and live jobs). AC14 wants failure artifacts genuinely published on a failed run; a failed run that also produces no evidence file (e.g. a crash before the runner ever writes e2e-verdict.json) still shows the upload step green — doesn't flip overall job status (the job already failed from the `set -o pipefail`-protected run step), but weakens the tamper/silent-gap trail an operator would use to diagnose why. Consider `error` instead of `warn`.

Found during FEAT-581 (TASK-3545) code review.

payload.title: runner.py and evidence.py independently recompute overlapping required-node pass/fail logic
payload.body:
`runner.py`'s `_verdict_status` and `evidence.py`'s `verify_evidence` independently recompute overlapping required-node pass/fail logic across two modules with no shared helper. Currently consistent (verified during FEAT-581 review), but a future edit to one could silently diverge from the other, producing a runner verdict and a verify_evidence disposition that disagree. Consider extracting the shared "required node -> pass/fail/blocked" computation into one helper both modules call.

Found during FEAT-581 code review.

payload.title: Live plan budget is not passed to the fixture agent
payload.body: run_plan creates only a placeholder _LiveBudgetContext and does not pass E2EPlan.budget into pytest or the mcp-agent target. The live test starts its own target, and live._ensure_agent calls build_live_generation_budget(opt_in) with LiveBudget defaults. Thus plan-level timeout/max-output/max-request limits do not control the paid run; e.g. live.md timeout_s=90 is enforced as the default 60, and per-plan changes have no effect. Propagate the validated plan budget into the child and construct one run-scoped GenerationBudget from it.

payload.title: 7 finance/crypto tool tests in core are permanently uncollectable after the ai-parrot-finance extraction
payload.body:
## What is wrong

Seven test modules under `packages/ai-parrot/tests/` import `parrot.tools.<x>` for finance/crypto tools that were extracted into a separate `ai-parrot-finance` distribution (`parrot.finance.tools.<x>`). That distribution is not a member of this uv workspace (`packages/ai-parrot-finance` does not exist), so the imports can never resolve here. Each file is a hard collection error.

| Test file | Import | Status of target |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cmc_fear_greed.py` | `parrot.tools.cmc_fear_greed` | deleted, no shim |
| `test_coingecko_toolkit.py` | `parrot.tools.coingecko` | deleted, no shim |
| `test_cointelegraph_tool.py` | `parrot.tools.cointelegraph` | deleted, no shim |
| `test_cryptoquant_toolkit.py` | `parrot.tools.cryptoquant` | deleted, no shim |
| `test_marketnews_tool.py` | `parrot.tools.marketnews` | deleted, no shim |
| `test_tradingeco_tool.py` | `parrot.tools.tradingeco` | deleted, no shim |
| `test_composite_score_tool.py` | `parrot.tools.composite_score` | migration shim exists |

The first six raise `ModuleNotFoundError`. `composite_score` is different: `packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/composite_score.py` is a migration shim that raises

```
ImportError: parrot_tools.composite_score has moved to parrot.finance.tools.composite_score (ai-parrot-finance).
```

so `parrot.tools.composite_score` still fails, just with a clearer message. `parrot_tools/__init__.py:229,233` already points `composite_score` and `technical_analysis` at `parrot.finance.tools.*`.

## Why it matters

These are 7 of the 26 collection errors that make `pytest packages/ai-parrot/tests` unrunnable as a whole. They are not caught by CI (`ci.yml` only runs `packages/ai-parrot/tests/docs/` from this tree, and its broad sweeps use `--continue-on-collection-errors`), so they accumulate silently — but they do cost agent runs: an sdd-worker on FEAT-603 halted on this error wall and misattributed it to its own task.

The tests themselves are dead weight either way: the code they exercise no longer lives in this repo, so they have not verified anything since the extraction.

## Suggested fix

Delete all seven files from `packages/ai-parrot/tests/`. Their coverage belongs with the code, in the `ai-parrot-finance` repo — confirm it was carried over there before deleting, and port it if not.

Do **not** "fix" them with `pytest.importorskip` or a skip marker: that hides a permanent relocation behind what reads like an optional-dependency skip.

Separately worth deciding: the six deleted modules have no migration shim while `composite_score` and `technical_analysis` do. Either add shims for the other six or drop the two that exist, so the extraction has one consistent story.

payload.title: test_chat_storage.py imports CONVERSATIONS_COLLECTION, removed from parrot.storage.chat
payload.body:
## What is wrong

`packages/ai-parrot/tests/test_chat_storage.py:23` imports `CONVERSATIONS_COLLECTION` from `parrot.storage.chat`:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'CONVERSATIONS_COLLECTION' from 'parrot.storage.chat'
  (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/storage/chat.py)
```

The name does not exist anywhere in `packages/*/src` any more. `chat.py` currently defines only `HOT_TTL_HOURS` (line 20), `DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT` (21) and `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TURNS` (22) — the collection-name constant was removed or inlined without updating the test.

The whole module fails at collection, so every test in it is lost, not just the two assertions that use the symbol (lines 351 and 376, both `assert call_args.args[0] == CONVERSATIONS_COLLECTION`).

## Why it matters

Unlike the finance/crypto tests filed alongside this one, `parrot.storage.chat` is **live core code that still exists**. This file is presumably meant to be covering it, and has silently covered nothing since the constant went away. The loss is invisible because CI does not collect `packages/ai-parrot/tests` as a whole.

## Suggested fix

Find what replaced the constant in `chat.py` — whether the collection name is now a literal at the call site, a config value, or an attribute on the storage class — and update the import and the two assertions to match. Then run the module on its own to confirm the rest of its tests still pass and still assert something meaningful:

```
pytest packages/ai-parrot/tests/test_chat_storage.py -q
```

If the collection name is now a literal inlined in `chat.py`, prefer re-introducing a module-level constant over hardcoding the string in the test, so the two cannot drift apart again.

payload.title: merge-tier validation collection errors abort whole distributions, unrelated to changed tasks
payload.body:
On FEAT-601's worktree (feat-FEAT-601-training-agent), running `coder_run_validation(tier="merge")` for TASK-3721/TASK-3726 selected and ran the FULL test suite of ~20 distributions (not scoped to changed files), and failed overall (exit_code=1) purely due to PRE-EXISTING, unrelated collection errors:

- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/shell_tool/test_command_rules.py` / `test_command_sanitizer.py` / `test_security_policy.py`: ImportError — `_default_command_rules`, `_DANGEROUS_PATTERNS`, `_DEFAULT_DENIED_COMMANDS` no longer exist in `parrot_tools.shell_tool.security` (renamed/removed by another feature, tests not updated). This aborted the ENTIRE `ai-parrot-tools` distribution ("Interrupted: 5 errors during collection"), so TASK-3721's own `test_assembly.py` never actually executed inside that run despite passing cleanly standalone.
- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/test_alpaca.py`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'parrot.tools.alpaca'`.
- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/test_zoom_interface.py`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'parrot.integrations.zoom'`.
- `packages/ai-parrot/tests/*` (26 collection errors: test_notification.py missing `aiohttp` dependency install, test_chat_storage.py, test_botmanager_flags.py, test_expense_approval.py FileNotFoundError, etc.) aborted the ENTIRE `ai-parrot` distribution ("Interrupted: 26 errors during collection"), so `packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/manuals/test_spikes.py` (TASK-3726) never actually executed either, despite passing cleanly standalone.
- Additional real (non-collection) failures unrelated to FEAT-601: ai-parrot-embeddings namespace surface drift (`UFormEmbedding` vs `UFormEmbeddingModel`), ai-parrot-client-grok multiround usage, ai-parrot-integrations telegram/matrix/voice-demo-browser suites, ai-parrot-loaders excel loader.

None of these failures/errors mention `assembly`, `spikes`, `procedures`, or `manuals` (verified via grep over the full validation log — zero matches). The merge-tier selector's scope for this feature branch (after ~26 already-merged tasks spanning many distributions) appears to expand to whole-distribution sweeps rather than the changed-files ∪ import-impact scope the tool description promises, so ANY task closure on a heavily-merged feature branch is blocked by this unrelated, pre-existing breakage — not just FEAT-601.

Suggested fix: (1) fix/skip the specific pre-existing collection errors (shell_tool test/source drift, missing alpaca/zoom modules, missing aiohttp dev dependency) so collection no longer aborts whole distributions; (2) audit why `tier="merge"` selected every distribution instead of a changed-scope subset for this feature branch — see also `merge-tier validation cost` (PR #1494 / FEAT-604) which reports a related but distinct "12 pre-existing dev_loop failures" symptom.

Full validation log: `artifacts/logs/sdd-coder-usage/executions/981de749-8a38-47ed-a033-752eb90afb12/background_logs/bf7f97ccf309789a032e9660b2849cf90b3409734a181244861a0f1ed7594e1e.log` (worktree feat-FEAT-601-training-agent).

FEAT-604 TASK-3801 xdist evidence measurement incomplete + wrong per-distribution timeout formula
payload.body:
TASK-3801 (xdist-evidence-spike) delivered real evidence (artifacts/logs/feat-604-xdist.md, git-ignored — add -f to view) and populated policy.py's XDIST_SAFE_DISTRIBUTIONS with 17 small, genuinely-verified-safe distributions. Two problems found in manual review:

1. The task specified a per-distribution wall-time cap of "~3x its expected serial time" (spec §3 M3 Implementation Notes / TASK-3801 Key Constraints), but the delivery used a flat 30s cap for every distribution. ai-parrot-loaders (421 tests, serial=19.57s, so a correct cap would be ~59s) was excluded at the 30s mark — likely a false negative, not a real xdist-safety problem. navrules (serial=0.68s) was also excluded at 30s under the same flat cap, though its correct 3x cap (~2s) would have been *tighter*, so that exclusion may still be legitimate (or may be the known post-summary-hang leaked-thread issue per pytest-unit-hangs-after-summary memory).

2. Only ~15 minutes of the task's own ~2h measurement budget was used. Seven in-scope distributions the spec explicitly calls out as cost-significant were never measured at all: `root` tests/ (520 files, "the second-largest cost driver" per spec §3 M3), `ai-parrot-tools` (310), `parrot-formdesigner` (226), `ai-parrot-embeddings`, `ai-parrot-pipelines`, `ai-parrot-visualizations`, `ai-parrot-client-google`. The evidence file's own resumable design (skip-finished-distributions) means a follow-up run can safely continue where this one stopped.

Suggested fix: re-run the M3 measurement (or a follow-up task) that (a) implements the 3x-serial-time cap instead of a flat 30s constant, and (b) continues through the remaining unmeasured in-scope distributions within the ~2h budget, re-evaluating ai-parrot-loaders and navrules with the corrected formula.

Recorded as coder-feedback:674fa764bafefeed67bf27df (model pattern: flat-timeout-instead-of-formula) and coder-review:0c948265c8b190b1d7702505.

payload.title: stale-mock-assertion-after-own-signature-change
ProcedureVerifier prose sanitizer has regex coverage gaps — unverified step/value claims can slip through
payload.body:
packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/procedures/verifier.py:21-22,162-183 (TASK-3722, FEAT-601). `_check_prose` is the ONLY enforcement of the module's own documented guarantee ("prose can never add a step, value or citation", AC7) for the free-text answer intro. Its two fixed regexes have real coverage gaps:

- `_STEP_NUM_RE = r"\b(?:step|paso)\s+(\d{1,3})\b"` only catches literal "step N"/"paso N" — "step three", "in the third step", or a bare "#3" reference are never examined.
- `_VALUE_RE` only recognizes a fixed unit whitelist (`n·m|nm|n-m|min|mm|kg`). A hallucinated value in ft-lb, psi, °C/°F, volts, or any bare number with no matched unit ("torque it to 45", "wait about 20") is released verbatim, unblocked.
- `test_verifier.py::test_verifier_prose_cannot_add_steps` only exercises the one covered unit ("N·m") — the gap itself is untested.

This does NOT compromise the structured `steps`/`citations`/`hazards` (those are fully evidence-gated and unaffected by this file) — only the free-text "answer" intro's own claimed guarantee is weaker than documented.

Suggested fix: either broaden the sanitizer to a stricter default-deny posture (block any prose containing a bare number/ordinal at all unless it exactly matches an already-released value), or add regex coverage for a wider unit set and word-form numbers, plus tests exercising the currently-uncovered cases.

payload.title: Guided-mode toolkit state (_guided dict) is non-durable across gunicorn workers; zero test coverage
payload.body:
packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/procedures/toolkit.py:48,258-374 (TASK-3724, FEAT-601, AC15).

1. Zero test coverage anywhere in packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/procedures/ for `start_guided`/`next_step`/`mark_done`/`resume_guided` (verified via grep across both test trees — only unrelated files matched). `test_guided.py` only tests the pure helpers `task_steps_for`/`record_completion` in guided.py; `test_toolkit.py` never touches guided mode. The claimed round-trip and "completion records WORKFLOW_PATTERN episode" behavior of the toolkit wiring itself is unverified.

2. `self._guided: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}` (line 48) is a plain in-process instance dict, not durable. `mark_done` hard-fails with `{"status": "not_found", "reason": "guided procedure state is unavailable"}` if `self._guided` lacks the `task_id` — which happens whenever the resuming request lands on a different `ProceduresToolkit`/`ProceduresAgent` instance (a gunicorn worker restart, a different worker in the pool, a new deploy) than the one that ran `start_guided`. This directly undercuts docs/knowledge/manuals.md §6's own claim ("`proc_resume`... so '¿dónde me quedé?' works the next day") — the durable `TaskAssociationStore`/task-memory state survives, but the richer per-step `AssembledProcedure`/label mapping the toolkit needs does not, and there's no rehydration path. Given the stack is gunicorn with multiple workers (per CLAUDE.md), this is a realistic production scenario.

Suggested fix: persist the guided-mode step mapping (or enough to rehydrate it) through the same durable task-memory store `start_guided` already writes to, and add toolkit-level tests for the full start_guided/next_step/mark_done/resume_guided round trip (not just the pure guided.py helpers).

payload.title: AC19's declared test command fails to collect (pre-existing multi-distribution pytest layout issue)
payload.body:
sdd/specs/training-agent.spec.md AC19's exact composite test command — `pytest packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/manuals packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/common packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/procedures packages/ai-parrot-integrations/tests -q` — fails to even collect when run verbatim: `ImportPathMismatchError: ('tests.conftest', '.../ai-parrot/tests/conftest.py', PosixPath('.../ai-parrot-integrations/tests/conftest.py'))`. This is a pre-existing multi-distribution pytest layout issue (each distribution's tests/ is a same-named top-level package colliding under pytest's default import mode) — not something FEAT-601 introduced, and not unique to this feature (any composite invocation crossing 2+ distributions' tests/ hits it). Running each directory separately, all suites pass (manuals+common 127 passed/3 skipped, procedures 40 passed, channel-delivery-matrix 4 passed).

Suggested fix: either add `--import-mode=importlib` to the declared AC19 command, or have SDD spec authors declare per-distribution test commands instead of one composite cross-distribution invocation.

payload.title: ProcedureAnswerKind has an unused "clarification" enum value; docs overstate audit coverage for Clarification
payload.body:
Two small, low-severity findings from the FEAT-601 pre-push review:

1. `ProcedureAnswerKind` includes a `"clarification"` literal (models.py:31) that `ProcedureAnswer` never actually constructs with — `Clarification` is always returned as its own separate Pydantic type throughout retrieval.py/service.py/agent.py. Harmless dead enum value worth pruning or documenting why it's reserved.

2. docs/knowledge/manuals.md §6 states "Audit row — every outcome, including denials," but `service.answer()`'s `needs_serial` `Clarification` path (and every other `Clarification` returned from `retrieval.plan()`/`resolve_equipment`/`resolve_procedure`) returns before reaching `_release()`, so no audit record is written for clarifications (confirmed by `test_needs_serial_returns_clarification`'s own `assert catalog.answers == []`). Likely intentional (a clarification request isn't itself an "answer"), but the docs slightly overstate "every outcome" — worth a one-line correction.
