tests/interfaces collection fails: test_file_shim.py ImportError under pytest (pre-existing, env-specific)
payload.body:
Running `pytest packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces` (the merge-tier mirror scope for anything touching `parrot/interfaces/file/*.py`, e.g. FEAT-603's graph.py) fails at COLLECTION time with:

```
ERROR collecting tests/interfaces/test_file_shim.py
ImportError: cannot import name 'FileManagerTool' from 'parrot.tools.filemanager' (unknown location)
```

`FileManagerTool` genuinely exists in `packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/tools/filemanager.py` (verified via a plain `python -c "from parrot.tools.filemanager import FileManagerTool"` with the same PYTHONPATH — succeeds and reports the correct worktree file). The failure is pytest-specific: it does not reproduce via a bare `python -c` import in the same environment/PYTHONPATH, only under `pytest -m ...` collection of `tests/interfaces` (reproduces even collecting `test_file_shim.py` alone). Root cause is not fully isolated but is consistent with the documented worktree gotcha in `.claude/rules/worktree-management.md` ("the shared .venv is editable-installed against the main checkout, so a bare pytest inside a worktree imports the wrong branch") interacting with `parrot/__init__.py`'s `pkgutil.extend_path` PEP-420 namespace merge and/or pytest's own sys.path rootdir insertion order — a stray `/home/jesuslara/proyectos/ai-parrot/agents` entry from the ambient PYTHONPATH was observed on sys.path during collection.

**Reproduced BEFORE FEAT-603/TASK-3753 existed**: checked out the per-spec index state as of TASK-3752 (commit f7fbb4ec5) in an isolated worktree and re-ran the identical pytest command — same collection error. This confirms the bug is pre-existing and environment-specific, not introduced by FEAT-603.

**Impact**: blocks the standard merge-tier validation selector for the WHOLE `packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces` directory whenever it is chosen as mirror/import-impact scope, for any task touching `parrot/interfaces/*` or `parrot/tools/filemanager.py`. Worked around for TASK-3753 by running its own declared test file in isolation (`pytest packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces/test_graph_filemanager.py` — 48 passed) as manual evidence instead of the directory-wide sweep.

**Suggested fix**: investigate whether `test_file_shim.py`'s collection order interacts badly with `parrot/__init__.py`'s `pkgutil.extend_path(__path__, __name__)` PEP-420 merge under pytest's "prepend" import-mode rootdir insertion, and/or whether an ambient `PYTHONPATH` entry (`/home/jesuslara/proyectos/ai-parrot/agents`) is leaking into worktree test runs and should be stripped/ordered after the worktree's own `packages/*/src` entries by the sdd-coder validation runner.

FEAT-604 qa.py cap-escalation writer plumbing is unreachable at tier=feature (QANode's only call site)
payload.body:
TASK-3799 extended nodes/qa.py::_record_green_escalations and _default_criteria to pass impact_files/impacted_hashes (cap escalation data) to record_green_escalation, per spec §3 Module 2's Integration Points row ("nodes/qa.py::_record_green_escalations — extends: same, for the dev-loop QA path").

However QANode's only call site of plan_tests uses tier="feature" (qa.py:597), and select.py's cap-detection block only computes cap_hits/cap_impacted `if index is not None and tier == "merge"` (select.py:175) — for tier="feature" these are always {}. So getattr(plan, "cap_hits", {}).get(dist, ()) at qa.py is always {}.get(dist, ()) in real usage: the new impact_files/impacted_hashes plumbing can never receive non-empty cap data from the actual plan_tests(tier="feature") call QANode makes. This matches plan_tests' own docstring ("feature=declared∪mirror∪core", explicitly not impact/cap).

The new test test_qa_records_cap_escalation_from_plan (test_qanode_feature_tier.py) passes only because it monkeypatches plan_tests to return a hand-constructed ScopePlan(tier="feature", cap_hits={...}) — a state the real function can never produce at that tier. So it proves the code doesn't crash on that input, not that the integration works end-to-end.

Not catastrophic (harmless dead code, not a wrong-write bug), and doesn't violate any AC (no AC requires feature-tier cap dedup). But the spec's own Integration Points table implies cap dedup extends to the QA path, which isn't actually true — either qa.py's feature-tier flow needs a way to produce cap hits (larger change touching select.py's tier gating), or this dead plumbing/test should be removed and the spec corrected to say cap dedup is merge-tier-only.

payload.title: FEAT-604 ScopePlan.cap_hits/cap_impacted are mutable dicts inside a frozen dataclass
payload.body:
datatypes.py's ScopePlan is @dataclass(frozen=True) with every other collection field (invocations, escalated, core_hits, skipped_escalations, notes) as an immutable tuple. FEAT-604's new cap_hits: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] and cap_impacted: dict[str, str] fields are plain mutable dicts, breaking the class's established immutability convention (frozen=True doesn't protect mutable dict contents). Low severity since nothing currently mutates a returned plan in place, but worth switching to an immutable mapping (or tuple-of-pairs) for consistency.

Related, lower-priority note from the same review: select.py's mirror-target filter for ledger-skipped cap distributions (the TASK-3798 review fix) only filters target.reason == "mirror". A reason == "declared" target for the same distribution (possible via select_tests.py's declared argv parsing, though not via background.py's own _plan_selection, which never passes declared) would survive and still produce an invocation despite the ledger skip. Probably fine (declared = explicit user intent should arguably always run), but worth a one-line comment confirming that's intentional if so.

payload.title: FEAT-604 nitpicks: dead I/O write, misleading criterion suffix, vacuous test assertion
payload.body:
Three low-severity nitpicks from FEAT-604's final adversarial code review (2026-09-25), bundled since each is a one-line, non-blocking cleanup:

1. background.py's empty-invocations branch does log_path.write_bytes(b"") immediately followed by _append_log(...) with the full header+message. The first write is dead I/O — _append_log opens in "a" mode and would create the file itself. Harmless, just redundant.

2. qa.py: the criterion-name suffix " (core escalation)" is now applied to cap/impact escalations too (via reason in ("core", "escalated")), which is misleading given cap escalations aren't core escalations. Since _record_green_escalations matches on this exact string, a rename to a tier-neutral " (escalation)" would be clearer without any behavior change — low priority since it's cosmetic and currently unreachable for cap anyway (see the separate major finding on qa.py dead code).

3. test_cap_escalation_ledger.py::test_plan_reports_cap_driving_files has `assert int(plan.cap_impacted["a"], 16) >= 0`, which is vacuously true for any valid hex string; the only real assertion is the length-64 check on the preceding line. Not misleading, just doesn't add coverage.

payload.body:
Running `pytest packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests` (merge-tier import-impact scope for anything touching
`parrot_tools/o365/*`) aborts at COLLECTION time with 5 unrelated errors, before any test in the directory
runs:

- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/shell_tool/test_command_rules.py` — `ImportError: cannot import name
  '_default_command_rules' from 'parrot_tools.shell_tool.security'`
- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/shell_tool/test_command_sanitizer.py` — `ImportError: cannot import name
  '_DANGEROUS_PATTERNS' from 'parrot_tools.shell_tool.security'`
- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/shell_tool/test_security_policy.py` — `ImportError: cannot import name
  '_DEFAULT_DENIED_COMMANDS' from 'parrot_tools.shell_tool.security'`
- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/test_alpaca.py` — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'parrot.tools.alpaca'`
- `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/test_zoom_interface.py` — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named
  'parrot.integrations.zoom'`

None of these are reachable from FEAT-603 (SharePoint/OneDrive FileManager) work: they are shell-tool security
internals and unrelated third-party integrations (Alpaca, Zoom). Reproduced identically across three separate
merge-tier validation runs while closing TASK-3762/TASK-3763/TASK-3766 in this feature (2026-09-25), all of which
only touch `parrot_tools/o365/*` and `docs/`. Manually scoped runs of the actual delivered test files
(`packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/test_o365_sharepoint_file_tools.py`,
`test_o365_onedrive_file_tools.py`, `test_o365_delta_tools.py`, `tests/tools/test_office365_toolkit.py`,
`packages/ai-parrot/tests/test_graph_filemanager_docs.py`) all pass (75 + 8 + 3 = 86 passed, 0 failed).

Same class of issue as ledger issue:71cbc792726c (a different pre-existing collection blocker in
`packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces`), suggesting either drifted `parrot_tools.shell_tool.security` internals
vs. its tests, or missing optional dependencies/modules (`parrot.tools.alpaca`, `parrot.integrations.zoom`) in
this environment that the test files assume are always present. Blocks the standard merge-tier validation
selector for the whole `ai-parrot-tools` distribution whenever any `parrot_tools.*` file is touched.

Suggested fix: either re-export the renamed/removed private names from `parrot_tools.shell_tool.security` that
its own tests expect, or mark `test_alpaca.py`/`test_zoom_interface.py` with an explicit skip/xfail if those
integrations are genuinely optional-dependency-gated and not installed in this environment.

`test_o365_onedrive_file_tools.py` (confirmed via git diff --stat on the feature branch). No task's
Completion Note records this as a deviation. Actual test coverage is fine (16/16 passing with real
assert set(result) == {...} key-set checks), but AC17 as literally written is unverifiable/false and
will mislead anyone trying to re-run it verbatim.

Suggested fix: update AC17's command in the spec (and any place it's echoed, e.g. docs) to name the
two real file names instead of the imagined refactor.py name.

payload.title: FEAT-603 introduces new blocking Path I/O inside async functions (ASYNC240)
payload.body:
CLAUDE.md / .claude/rules/codebase-conventions.md forbid blocking I/O in async code. FEAT-603 gets
this right in graph.py's upload_file (uses `await asyncio.to_thread(local_path.stat)`), but introduces
new, avoidable blocking `pathlib.Path` calls (`.stat()`, `.exists()`) directly inside `async def` in
several new code paths added by this same feature (confirmed via `git diff` + `ruff check --select
ASYNC240` that these are new lines, not pre-existing context):
- packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/tools/filemanager.py — new `_batch_upload`/`batch_upload` bodies in
  both FileManagerTool and FileManagerToolkit (dest_path.stat(), source_path.exists()/.stat()).
- packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/o365/sharepoint.py:396 (and an unflagged ternary form).
- packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/o365/onedrive.py:265,276,309.

Low real-world severity (cheap local stat calls), but avoidable and inconsistent with the pattern the
same PR uses correctly elsewhere.

Suggested fix: wrap these calls in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` like graph.py's upload_file does.

payload.title: FEAT-603 out-of-scope pure reformatting diff in onedrive.py
payload.body:
packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/interfaces/onedrive.py: roughly 150-220 of the ~220 changed lines are
pure black-style reformatting (quote-style changes, backslash-continuations converted to parens)
across methods this feature never intended to touch (_ensure_folder, file_list, file_search,
download_file, upload_folder, etc.). Spec Module 2 scopes this file to an additive ~45-line change
only (the new _user_drives cache + _resolve_user_drive, roughly :48-62 and :88-106). Confirmed
independently by 3 of 5 review passes during FEAT-603's adversarial review.

Violates .claude/rules/codebase-conventions.md's "minimal, focused diffs — touch only the files your
task lists" and needlessly inflates merge-conflict surface on a file the spec itself calls
"modifies (additive)".

Suggested fix: in a follow-up, revert the unrelated reformatting hunks in onedrive.py, keeping only
the additive _user_drives/_resolve_user_drive changes, so the file's history stays legible.

payload.title: FEAT-603 signature-snapshot guard test only checks one direction (AC19 gap)
payload.body:
packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces/test_feat603_guards.py::test_public_signatures_unchanged iterates
the CURRENT source's methods and looks each up `if key in signatures` (the recorded baseline), but
never verifies that every snapshotted baseline key is still present in the current source. A renamed
or removed pre-existing public method on SharepointClient/OneDriveClient/O365Client/FileManagerTool/
FileManagerToolkit/the O365 toolkits would silently escape detection by this guard, defeating part of
AC19's "no breaking change" intent. Verified by reading the test code directly; no evidence any method
was actually removed by this feature — this is a test-completeness gap, not a live production bug.

Suggested fix: add the reverse check — for every key in the baseline snapshot, assert it is still
present in the current source's signature map.

payload.title: FEAT-603 AC2 text doesn't account for the client_class override
payload.body:
Spec AC2 says SharePointFileManager/OneDriveFileManager "differ from the base only by manager_name,
__init__, _build_client and _resolve_drive_id" — but both also declare a `client_class` attribute
(sharepoint.py:23, onedrive.py:21), which is load-bearing (graph.py:323's adopt_client does
isinstance(client, self.client_class)). This is a legitimate 5th override the AC's literal text
misses. Not a code defect; recommend updating the AC wording rather than treating it as a bug.

payload.title: FEAT-603 AC14 missing recorded install-log evidence
payload.body:
AC14 explicitly requires that `uv pip install -e "packages/ai-parrot[msgraph]"` resolving be recorded
under artifacts/logs/. The pyproject.toml msgraph extra itself is correct and complete, but no log file
evidences the install was actually run. Suggested fix: run the install once and save its output under
artifacts/logs/ per AC14.

payload.title: FEAT-603 GraphDriveFileManager._classify never produces BatchErrorCode.permission_denied
payload.body:
BatchErrorCode declares "permission_denied" (parrot/interfaces/file/batch.py) but
GraphDriveFileManager._classify() (graph.py) never returns it — only "auth" is produced for
PermissionError. Dead enum value; either _classify should distinguish 401 (auth) from 403
(permission_denied), or the unused enum member should be removed/documented as reserved.

payload.title: FEAT-603 upload conflict_behavior/small-file-threshold interaction undocumented
payload.body:
graph.py's small-file-vs-upload-session routing is gated on `conflict_behavior == "replace"`
(graph.py:742,759) — for "fail"/"rename", even tiny files go through the slower chunked-session path
(a legitimate constraint: Graph's simple content-PUT endpoint has no conflictBehavior parameter). This
side effect is not documented in docs/interfaces/graph-filemanager.md, which only describes the
conflict-behavior options themselves, not this routing interaction. Suggested fix: add a sentence to
the docs explaining that fail/rename conflict behaviors always use the upload-session path regardless
of file size.

payload.title: FEAT-603 _GuardedFileServingExtension swallows exceptions with no logging
payload.body:
graph.py's _GuardedFileServingExtension.handle_file (~lines 69-77) does `except Exception: pass`
around the size-guard's metadata fetch with no logging at all before falling through to the
underlying extension. This masks unexpected errors (auth failures, transient Graph errors), not just
the expected 404 case, contrary to this project's logging convention (self.logger.* instead of
silent pass). Suggested fix: log the exception at debug/warning level before falling through.

payload.title: FEAT-603 spec commentary on batch cancellation summary doesn't match implementation
payload.body:
Spec Module 1's docstring commentary for upload_files says cancellation results are "still returned by
the toolkit summary as aborted" — but FileManagerToolkit.batch_upload/batch_download never catch
CancelledError to build a partial summary; cancellation just propagates (which is correct per AC8's
literal text and asyncio best practice). This is a documentation/implementation mismatch in the spec's
prose, not an AC violation — the code is correct, the spec commentary is stale/aspirational.
Suggested fix: correct the spec's Module 1 commentary to match the actual (correct) propagate-don't-
catch behavior.

payload.title: FEAT-603 DownloadOneDriveFileTool duplicates response-dict block across branches
payload.body:
packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/o365/onedrive.py:
DownloadOneDriveFileTool._execute_graph_operation duplicates the same download+response-dict-building
block in both its file_id and file_path branches instead of factoring it into a single shared tail.
Purely a maintainability nitpick — behavior is correct and tested. Suggested fix: extract the shared
tail into a small private helper.

payload.title: FEAT-603 six ruff B023 loop-variable-binding findings in graph.py closures
payload.body:
6x ruff B023 (loop-variable binding) findings in graph.py's pagination/upload closures. Traced as
false positives during FEAT-603's adversarial review — each closure runs synchronously within the
same loop iteration it's defined in, so the classic late-binding bug doesn't actually apply — but
they're fragile against future refactors (e.g. if someone later defers execution via asyncio.gather
or a stored callback list). Suggested fix: add `# noqa: B023` with a one-line comment explaining why
it's safe at each site, so a future refactor that breaks the safety assumption gets re-flagged by
ruff instead of silently inheriting a stale suppression.

payload.title: FEAT-603 minor nitpicks: bare assert, stale comment, extra round-trip, snapshot metadata
payload.body:
Four trivial nitpicks from FEAT-603's adversarial review, bundled since each is standalone/very low
risk:
1. packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/interfaces/file/sharepoint.py — SharePointFileManager._build_client
   uses a bare `assert client._srcfiles == []` (stripped under `python -O`) for a correctness invariant

4. packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces/feat603_signature_snapshot.json — the recorded base_commit
   field doesn't match the actual base commit (cosmetic only; the sha256 guards it protects still pass
   genuinely against the real base).

None block anything; listed together for future cleanup convenience.

payload.title: wikitoolkit ledger close refuses every issue with 'missing or status=None'
payload.body:
`wikitoolkit ledger close <issue_id> --reason ... --actor ...` fails for
EVERY issue tested (both FEAT-603's own newly-filed issues and an unrelated
pre-existing issue `issue:0974a2a92df3`), always with:

```
[WARNING] parrot.knowledge.wiki.ledger.service(service.py:261) :: Refusing issue.closed for <id>: missing or status=None
Could not close <id>
```

Reproduced after `wikitoolkit ledger sync` and `wikitoolkit ledger rebuild`
(both succeed, neither fixes it). `wikitoolkit ledger claim <id>` on the same
ids also fails with "already claimed or closed" even though `wikitoolkit
ledger ready` lists them as open/unclaimed — suggesting the read path
(`ready`) and the write/state-check path (`claim`/`close`, in
`parrot/knowledge/wiki/ledger/service.py` around line 261) disagree about
an issue's current status, likely a stale or missing `status` field read
from the ledger's SQLite-backed index (`.parrot/ledger/ledger.db`) versus
its append-only event log (audit shows `issue.claimed: 18`, `issue.closed:
22` events already recorded, yet `service.py:261`'s check treats the
target issue's resolved status as `None`).

Impact: 12 confirmed-fixed findings from the FEAT-603 code review
(`issue:a4fcb388b194`, `7b64abab826a`, `f80c5b7ae8e4`, `304c8d9ba908`,
`3daf42eb6bec`, `3e6f18680665`, `5d0766d3e932`, `48fc752bb45e`,
`20d97ccac452`, `f8788122ef1e`, `74eca8ca3592`, `48b4a6356944`) could not be
closed despite their fixes being implemented, tested, committed and pushed
(PR #1501, commit 65da5cb17) — they remain stuck `open` in the ledger.

Suggested fix: audit `service.py`'s `issue.closed` handler (~line 261) for
how it resolves an issue's current `status` before accepting a close/claim
transition — it likely reads from a projection that isn't correctly
populated by `sync`/`rebuild` for issues opened via the `ledger_open` MCP
tool (as opposed to the CLI), or has an off-by-one/stale-cache bug in the
index reader.

payload.title: parrot-formdesigner control-registry tests are order-dependent under pytest-xdist (-n auto)
payload.body:
Discovered while completing FEAT-604's xdist safety evidence (issue:dd35b0648576): a genuine per-test-outcome measurement (1 serial + 2x `-n auto` runs, junitxml diff) on `packages/parrot-formdesigner/tests` found 8 real disagreements, all in `tests.unit.controls.test_control_registry_capabilities.TestBuiltinControlCapabilities`:
test_all_builtin_controls_present, test_container_controls_have_limited_effects, test_nps_likert_ranking_are_numeric, test_numeric_control_has_arithmetic_operations, test_numeric_control_has_comparison_operators, and 3 more in the same class — same set of tests flipped in BOTH xdist runs vs serial, consistently.

This is consistent with a shared, mutable control-registry singleton whose population order/state differs depending on which xdist worker collects/imports it first, not measurement noise (reproduced identically across 2 independent xdist runs). `parrot-formdesigner` is correctly excluded from `XDIST_SAFE_DISTRIBUTIONS` for this reason (see artifacts/logs/feat-604-xdist.md), but the underlying test isolation bug is a separate, real defect worth its own investigation and fix so this distribution can eventually be added.

Suggested fix: identify the shared registry (likely a module-level dict/singleton the control system builds at import time) and either make its population deterministic/idempotent regardless of import order, or give each test process-isolated state via a fixture reset.

payload.title: ai-parrot-tools academic research tests bleed rate-limiter/session state across xdist workers
payload.body:
Discovered while completing FEAT-604's xdist safety evidence (issue:dd35b0648576): a genuine per-test-outcome measurement on `packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests` found 7 real disagreements between serial and `-n auto` (reproduced identically in both independent xdist runs), all in `research/test_academic_*`:
test_academic_crossref.TestCrossref::test_uses_bibliographic_query, test_uses_polite_pool, test_academic_details.TestGetPaperDetails::test_explicit_source_overrides, test_s2_paper_lookup_url, test_academic_pubmed.TestPubMed::test_two_step_workflow, and 2 more.

Consistent with a shared rate-limiter or HTTP session object (likely module-level or process-global) whose state (call counters, cached politeness/backoff windows) is order-dependent across xdist workers that partition tests differently than serial collection order. `ai-parrot-tools` is correctly excluded from `XDIST_SAFE_DISTRIBUTIONS` for this reason (see artifacts/logs/feat-604-xdist.md).

Suggested fix: scope the rate-limiter/session fixture per-test (or per-worker) instead of module/process-global, or explicitly reset its state in a fixture teardown.

payload.title: root tests/unit/integrations/oauth2 leaks a closed asyncio event loop across xdist workers
payload.body:
Discovered while completing FEAT-604's xdist safety evidence (issue:dd35b0648576): a genuine per-test-outcome measurement on root `tests/` found 7 real disagreements between serial and `-n auto` (reproduced identically in both independent xdist runs), all in `tests.unit.integrations.oauth2.*`: test_handler, test_hydration, test_jira_provider, test_models, test_persistence, and 2 more.

The serial run's own log shows `parrot.integrations.oauth2: 8 module(s) skipped` (a collection-time skip, presumably an optional-dependency guard) together with `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` appearing in BOTH the serial and xdist logs — consistent with a shared/module-level asyncio event loop reference that one test (or worker) closes while another test still holds a reference to it, producing different collection/skip or pass/fail outcomes depending on execution order and worker assignment. This is a real async-fixture-lifecycle bug in the oauth2 integration test suite, not measurement noise. `root` is correctly excluded from `XDIST_SAFE_DISTRIBUTIONS` for this reason (see artifacts/logs/feat-604-xdist.md).

Suggested fix: audit the oauth2 test module/fixtures for a shared event-loop reference (e.g. a module-level client or session created once and reused across tests) and switch to a per-test or per-worker fixture scope, matching how other async test suites in this repo already isolate their event loops.

payload.reason: Completed the xdist safety measurement with the correct ~3x-serial-time per-distribution cap (was a flat 30s constant): re-measured ai-parrot-loaders/navrules as safe, measured the 7 remaining in-scope distributions (4 safe, 3 genuinely unsafe on real per-test disagreements), XDIST_SAFE_DISTRIBUTIONS now 23 entries, all in-scope distributions measured or pre-excluded on cited evidence.

payload.title: FEAT-598 merge-tier validation blast-radius pulls in ~2800 unrelated tests with pre-existing failures
payload.body:
The `parrot-sdd-coder` merge-tier validation (`coder_run_validation(tier="merge")`) for FEAT-598 tasks TASK-3769 and TASK-3779 — both scoped to `packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/outputs/a2ui/linked/*` and `packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/tools/dataset_manager/sources/query_slug.py` respectively — selects and runs a huge, apparently blast-radius-derived test set spanning nearly every distribution in the monorepo (ai-parrot, ai-parrot-integrations, ai-parrot-server, ai-parrot-tools, ai-parrot-visualizations, parrot-formdesigner, root).

Both runs failed with the IDENTICAL 37 failures in `packages/parrot-formdesigner/tests/` (e.g. `test_version_and_docs.py::test_version_bumped` expects version '0.9.0' but package is now '1.0.6'; `test_field_schema_snippets_cover_all_types`), plus `ERROR`s in `packages/ai-parrot-embeddings/tests/test_wheel_layout.py` (an `_pytest.pathlib.ImportPathMismatchError` conftest collision when formdesigner and embeddings tests run in the same session), plus transient xdist flakiness in `packages/ai-parrot-visualizations/tests/outputs/a2ui_renderers/*` (a `KeyError: OutputMode.STRUCTURED_CHART` / `No renderer registered` that reproduces ~0% of the time when the same file set is run standalone).

I verified representative failures directly against a clean `packages/ai-parrot/.venv` checkout on `dev` (no FEAT-598 changes applied):
- `test_version_and_docs.py::test_version_bumped` — FAILS on clean dev too (pre-existing, package version drifted past the test's hardcoded expectation).
- `test_field_schema_snippets_cover_all_types` — FAILS on clean dev too.
- `test_wheel_layout.py` standalone — PASSES (15/15); only fails when collected alongside `parrot-formdesigner/tests/` in the same pytest session (conftest path collision, a test-infra issue, not a real regression).
- The visualizations `test_structured_envelope.py::test_route_envelope_sets_a2ui_envelope` failure reproduced once, then passed both standalone and in the same 21-file group on both `dev` and the FEAT-598 worktree — confirmed flaky, not diff-caused.

Neither TASK-3769 nor TASK-3779 touch `parrot-formdesigner`, `ai-parrot-embeddings`, or any renderer registration code, so none of this is attributable to their diffs. This means EVERY task in FEAT-598 (28 tasks) will likely hit this same red merge-tier gate, making the gate's outcome useless as a per-task signal for this feature. Suggested fix: either scope the merge-tier selector's blast-radius expansion more tightly for `outputs/a2ui/linked/*` changes, or exclude `parrot-formdesigner`'s known-stale version/schema tests, and stop collecting `ai-parrot-embeddings` + `parrot-formdesigner` test trees in the same pytest session (fixes the conftest path collision).

payload.title: dsl.ts (TASK-3793) missing all import/export statements — applyTransform/TransformError undefined
payload.body:
packages/ai-parrot-server/ui/src/lib/components/agents/canvas/a2ui/linked/dsl.ts has zero `import`/`export` statements (verified via grep -c "export"/"^import" -> 0/0). It references Row, Op, and `throw new TransformError(...)` throughout but never imports or defines them. dsl.test.ts (also TASK-3793) imports `{ applyTransform, TransformError }` from './dsl', neither of which exists as a named export in the file.

Under Vite/Vitest's SSR module transform (vite-node), a missing named export resolves to `undefined` rather than throwing at import time, so module loading itself doesn't break — but any real call to `applyTransform` (e.g. a linked source with `transform.ops` set) will throw `TypeError: applyTransform is not a function` at runtime. TASK-3795's `linked/index.ts` (which correctly imports `{ applyTransform, TransformError }` from './dsl' per its own Codebase Contract) only invokes `applyTransform` when a source's `transform.ops` is present, so this path is presently non-functional end-to-end.

Discovered while implementing TASK-3795 (createLinkedLane / A2UISurface wiring), which is explicitly out of scope for touching dsl.ts ("NOT in scope: DSL/conditions (TASK-3793)" per its task file).

Suggested fix: add the missing `export function applyTransform(...)`/`export class TransformError extends Error {...}` (and any `Row`/`Op` type imports/definitions) to dsl.ts so the named exports dsl.test.ts and linked/index.ts already depend on actually exist. Also recommend running the real `vitest`/`tsc` suite once `node_modules` is available in a worktree — no worktree in this feature run had it installed, so this defect wasn't caught until a downstream task actually inspected the file's exports.

payload.reason: Fixed: ported the missing TransformError class + applyTransform orchestrator into dsl.ts from the Python reference executor (dsl.py), reusing generated Row/TransformOp/TransformSpec types. Verified with esbuild syntax check + 118/118 packages/ai-parrot/tests/outputs/a2ui/linked passed; real vitest/tsc still unverified (no node_modules in this sandbox) — recommend a CI run confirms.

payload.title: Review TASK-3847
A2UISurface.linked.test.ts: 4/6 tests fail on clean dev with svelte effect_update_depth_exceeded
payload.body: Found during FEAT-610 TASK-3845. Running `pnpm exec vitest run src/lib/components/agents/canvas/a2ui/A2UISurface.linked.test.ts` in packages/ai-parrot-server/ui on clean dev (main checkout, node_modules present) gives 4 failed | 2 passed. Error: 'Maximum update depth exceeded ... effect reads and writes the same piece of state' (svelte.dev/e/effect_update_depth_exceeded). Failing: 'fetches once on mount with the viewer bearer', 'a 404 keeps the snapshot and shows unavailable never denied', 'shows a loading notice while snapshot_at is null', 'a FilterBar filter with parrot_param re-fetches only that source'. payload.title: /sdd-done Step 9.1 ledger snapshot silently commits nothing (ledger export ignores cwd)
payload.body:
Step 9.1 of /sdd-done (and its .agent/workflows twin and .agents/skills/sdd-done/SKILL.md) creates a throwaway worktree at origin/<BASE> and runs:

    EXPORT_OUTPUT=$(cd "$TEMP_WORKTREE" && wikitoolkit ledger export 2>&1)

then `git -C "$TEMP_WORKTREE" add sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl` and commits.

`wikitoolkit ledger export` does NOT honour cwd — the ledger resolves to the
primary checkout, so the export always writes
`<MAIN_ROOT>/sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl`. The throwaway worktree therefore stays
clean, `git commit` fails with "nothing to commit", and the subsequent
`git push origin HEAD:<BASE>` pushes the unchanged detached HEAD and SUCCEEDS.
The recipe then prints "Ledger snapshot updated with changed issues." The
snapshot is never committed, and the export silently dirties
`sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl` in the SHARED primary checkout.

Observed during FEAT-619 closeout, 2026-10-01: export reported
"Exported sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl (changed)" and the step reported success,
yet origin/dev contained none of the six issues just closed.

The command already has the fix available: `wikitoolkit ledger export --dest
<path>`. Re-running with
`wikitoolkit ledger export --dest "$TEMP_WORKTREE/sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl"`
produced a real diff, a real commit and a real push.

Impact: every feature closed with /sdd-done since Step 9.1 was introduced may
have skipped its ledger snapshot while reporting success, and each left the
primary checkout with a dirty issues.jsonl. The `*"(changed)"*` guard cannot
catch this because export genuinely did change a file — just not the one being
committed.

Suggested fix: pass --dest explicitly, and make the step fail loudly (not
silently continue) when `git commit` finds nothing staged after export reported
"(changed)". Update all three copies: .claude/commands/sdd-done.md,
.agent/workflows/sdd-done.md, .agents/skills/sdd-done/SKILL.md.

payload.title: Transitive source_fanin makes leaf modules "core", escalating all 26 distributions on a merge-tier plan
payload.body:
Measured 2026-10-01 in worktree feat-FEAT-618 at base 275a8d2bd.

A merge-tier plan for a diff confined to a single leaf module,
packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/outputs/a2ui/linked/dsl.py, yields:

  core_hits: [(".../outputs/a2ui/linked/dsl.py", 26)]
  cap_hits keys: []
  invocations: 26 - one per distribution, including parrot-formdesigner
  and ai-parrot-embeddings, which the diff cannot affect.

cap_hits is EMPTY, so the impact cap contributes nothing. The entire
blast radius reported in issue:181bd0c01bb4 (~2800 tests) comes from
detect_core().

Mechanism: source_fanin() (impact.py:244-260) walks importers
TRANSITIVELY. A leaf module imported by a hub that is itself imported
across the monorepo therefore inherits the hub fan-in, clears
core_fanin_threshold, and escalates every distribution it transitively
reaches as reason="core". Fan-in measured here is 26 distributions for
what is a self-contained A2UI DSL module.

FEAT-618 TASK-3909 added ScopePolicy.escalate_foreign_dists to guard the
cap path; verified that the guard changes this plan NOT AT ALL (plans are
byte-identical with it on and off), because the cap path is inert here.
The guard is still correct for cap-driven escalation and is merged.

Open question for whoever takes this: is transitive fan-in the right core
signal at all? A direct-importer count, or a fan-in measured only across
distribution boundaries, would not promote a leaf DSL module to core.
Alternatively core escalation could respect the same
foreign-distribution/red-baseline policy the cap path now has.

payload.reason: Not resolved. SDD lane provisioned (FEAT-618: spec rev 0.3, TASK-3908..3914, worktree, branch pushed) and TASK-3909 merged, but its AC4 is unmet: measured on the real repo the blast radius is core-driven (core_hits=[(dsl.py,26)], cap_hits={}), not cap-driven, so the cap guard changes nothing here. Real root cause filed as issue:7f2f3d4d7828 (transitive source_fanin). TASK-3908 also blocked pending a strategy decision: deleting the 25 top-level tests/__init__.py moves the collision down to `unit` (shared by 19 distributions); the working fix is 262 deletions across every test tree. Releasing for a human scope decision.

FEAT-617 (PR #1538) landed substantial progress but did NOT satisfy the close criteria: none of this issue's three declared files appear in the diff, and all three still error. 18 -> 3 collection errors, 22873 -> 23090 tests collected. The issue's stated cause was wrong: conftest stubs accounted for 1 of 18 errors, not 14; the real cause is 8 test modules assigning sys.modules[...] at module scope without restoring (table in sdd/specs/manager-test-bot-cleanup-lifecycle-fixes.spec.md section 8b). payload.title: 3 collection errors survive FEAT-617; 2 are residual sys.modules pollution of an uncharacterised shape
payload.body:
FEAT-617 (PR #1538) took packages/ai-parrot/tests from 18 to 3 collection errors by
restoring modules that a test module shadowed at import scope. Three remain:

1. test_botmanager_flags.py and unit/scripts/test_recompute_contextual_embeddings.py
   COLLECT CLEANLY IN ISOLATION but fail in the full-tree sweep. The snapshot/restore
   hook in packages/ai-parrot/tests/conftest.py only restores entries a module
   REPLACED with a stub carrying no __file__; these two are poisoned by something of a
   different shape (a module deleted from sys.modules, replaced by a real-looking
   object, or parrot.__path__ mutation by the root conftest.py:140-157).
2. manager/test_bot_cleanup_lifecycle.py fails even in isolation on
   ModuleNotFoundError parrot.handlers.crew.execution_history_handler. That module
   exists (packages/ai-parrot-server/src/parrot/handlers/crew/) and imports fine via a
   plain python -c with the right PYTHONPATH, so this is namespace wiring under pytest,
   not a defect in the test.

Method that worked, for whoever picks this up: delta-debugging over the collected file
list to find a minimal poisoning prefix, then a per-victim scan of every module that
writes to sys.modules. Both scripts and the full polluter table are in
sdd/specs/manager-test-bot-cleanup-lifecycle-fixes.spec.md section 8b.

payload.title: retry-path-hits-dedup-before-resume
inbox dry-run does not validate archive/markdown destinations, so it can report success for a run that would fail
payload.body: InboxProcessor.process_one (inbox/processor.py) dry-run path runs triage/classify/link planning but never calls archive_destination or checks the markdown path, whose safety checks (_safe_stamp, rejected_subdir) only run on the real path. An unsafe inbox.date_format or rejected_subdir would still show dry_run success. Suggested fix: call archive_destination (pure path arithmetic) in dry-run and report the error as failed. From FEAT-626 code review finding 4.

payload.title: archive_original: os.replace can overwrite a destination created between the lexists check and the move
payload.body: inbox/archive.py archive_original checks os.path.lexists(destination) then os.replace(); replace silently overwrites, so a non-lock writer racing in between breaks the 'never overwritten' claim (AC9). The run lock makes this unlikely for inbox processes. Fix: exclusive create via os.link then unlink (with shutil fallback on EXDEV), or retry archive_destination on FileExistsError. From FEAT-626 code review finding 6.

payload.title: inbox processor: failure statuses and cost — bad discard manifest reports 'rejected' (exit 0); archive failure after admission reports 'failed'; _existing_doc_id scans all pages per document
payload.body: FEAT-626 code review findings 7-9 in inbox/processor.py: (7) process_one returns status='rejected' with an error when the discard manifest check fails, but the CLI exit code only follows report.failed, so it is silent; use 'failed'. (8) A failure inside _archive after verification succeeded makes run() report the document 'failed' although pages were admitted; consider reporting 'admitted' with a warning. (9) _existing_doc_id and the authored-page scan call store.dump_pages() for every document (O(pages x docs)); use a targeted lookup or a per-run cache. Nits: _doc_id_from_source is async without I/O; the except BaseException: pass in _inbox_write_lock could log at debug; triage.py/export.py contain black-only rewrapping that widens the FEAT-626 diff.

GoogleDriveToolkit.upload_file reads arbitrary local paths; conflict_behavior mutated on shared manager
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/google/drive.py upload_file: source_path is any local file an LLM-driven agent names (e.g. ~/.ssh/*) and is uploaded to Drive without a base-dir allowlist; fix by restricting to a configured root or reusing FileManagerTool's size/dir policy. Also conflict_behavior is flipped on the shared manager instance across awaits, so concurrent calls can leak a per-call fail/rename into another upload; pass as parameter instead. share_file also lets an agent create 'anyone' links — consider an allowed_share_scopes guard. Found in FEAT-608 code review.

payload.title: gdrive: download retry can duplicate bytes in BinaryIO sink; resumable chunk 429 ignores Retry-After
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/interfaces/file/gdrive.py ~L637-640: files_download(pipe_to=_AsyncSink(destination)) runs inside _retrying, so a 5xx/429 mid-stream retries and appends the same bytes to the caller's stream again; retry only when nothing written or tell()/truncate() back to start offset (delete partial Path file). Resumable _put (~L781-788) raises without .res so Retry-After isn't honoured on chunk 429s (AC8). Found in FEAT-608 code review.

FEAT-636: per-source data endpoint runs under owner pctx for any share-token holder who is not owner/scope-granted
payload.body: ui_surfaces.py:_source_data computes share_only = bool(token) and record.user_id != user_id and not (scope and scope_grants(...)). An authenticated user who is neither owner nor scope-granted but presents a valid ?share= token therefore runs under the OWNER principal context, bypassing their own PBAC. Spec §2/AC8 reads as viewer pctx for an authenticated viewer and owner pctx only for a share viewer with no JWT; _refresh uses owner pctx unconditionally, so the two readings conflict. Decide the intended rule (probably user_id is None) and return the access reason from resolve_surface_access instead of re-deriving it. Add tests for the authenticated non-scope token-holder case. Reviewer finding, spot-checked at ui_surfaces.py:776.

payload.title: FEAT-636: build-time probe runs python transformers on a 1-row frame; fetch_source truncation flag is imprecise
payload.body: (a) execute_sources(probe=True), used by toolkit.py build_linked_surface/dashboard, goes through the python branch of _run_source with a 1-row frame, so a valid transformer needing several rows or failing on tiny/empty input fails the build with transform_failed. Either fully fetch python sources when probing or skip the transform in probe mode and rely on validate_python_transform. (b) service.fetch_source sets truncated=len(rows) >= max_fetch_rows (true when exactly at the cap) and ignores the executor's own truncated flag; a transformer that aggregates sees input silently limited by querylimit with no warning. (c) No timeout around asyncio.to_thread in pytransform.apply_python_transform. (d) Missing endpoint tests: unknown key 404, wrong-surface token, truncation/cap. (e) 422 transform errors return the generic "Data source unavailable" message. Reviewer findings, not individually verified.

payload.title: Admin UI blocks non-Excel uploads at the picker and discards the upload response
payload.body:
`DataManagementModal.svelte:111` rejects client-side anything that is not `.xlsx`/`.xls` ("Only Excel files (.xlsx, .xls) are allowed."), so a `.docx` or `.pdf` can never be uploaded through the admin UI even after FEAT-639 makes the backend persist it.

Separately, `uploadAgentData` (`packages/ai-parrot-server/ui/src/lib/api/agent.ts:155-166`) PUTs the multipart body to `/api/v1/agents/chat/{agent}` — the handler FEAT-639 changes — and `DataManagementModal.svelte:122` awaits it and then shows a hardcoded "Uploaded", discarding the response entirely. No code anywhere reads `added_files` (audited across .py/.ts/.svelte/.js), so FEAT-639's hard cut of the response shape does not break the UI; it simply leaves the UI unable to surface what was actually stored or what failed.

Why it matters: FEAT-639 §8 Q3 was resolved as "backend now, UI in a separate feature". Without this follow-up, the admin UI remains a fourth silent gate on the very use case FEAT-639 exists to fix, and the user still gets a success message that is not derived from the server's answer.

Suggested fix: drop the extension allowlist in `DataManagementModal.svelte` (or widen it to the formats the session store accepts), and render FEAT-639's new upload response — stored files, registered dataframes, and per-file errors — instead of the fixed "Uploaded" string.

test_drive_toolkit.py sys.path.insert(0) shadows PyPI `jira` for all later-collected tools tests
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/google/test_drive_toolkit.py:12-13 does a module-scope sys.path.insert(0, packages/ai-parrot/tests/interfaces). That dir contains a `jira/` test package (with __init__.py), so every module collected afterwards that does `from jira import JIRA` (test_jira_config, test_jiratoolkit_envelope, unit/test_jiratoolkit_{delegation,oauth,verify_credentials,templates_config}) fails with "cannot import name 'JIRA' from 'jira' (.../ai-parrot/tests/interfaces/jira/__init__.py)". Each file passes when run alone, so only whole-directory runs (the merge-tier gate) hit it. Reproduced on clean origin/dev. Found by bisecting with a pytest plugin that reports the first collector at which sys.path is polluted. Fix: import _gdrive_fakes via importlib from its file path, or insert, import, then remove the path entry (or append instead of insert(0)). Separately, tests/google/test_calendar.py fails with "'parrot.interfaces.file' is not a package" because the root conftest.py stubs parrot.interfaces.file and only test_drive_toolkit pops that stub, and it is collected after test_calendar. payload.title: Review TASK-4117
JiraToolkit templates: missing-variable check is shallow, sync, and runs on every render
payload.body: jiratoolkit.py JiraToolkit._assert_template_variables parses only the template's own source (jinja2.meta.find_undeclared_variables on engine.env.parse(source)). (1) Variables used in {% include %}/{% extends %} targets are not checked, so such a template fails inside engine.render with UndefinedError, which TemplateEngine.render re-raises as ValueError/RuntimeError, not JiraTemplateError (AC8 'names every missing variable' is lost for included templates; no Jira call happens). (2) loader.get_source + env.parse are synchronous file I/O and CPU work in an async path on every render, and the compiled-template cache is not used. Fix: cache the undeclared-variable set per template name (invalidate on loader uptodate), recurse into referenced templates, and wrap UndefinedError into JiraTemplateError. Also: a template whose context value is None renders 'None' (call_fields always carry None for omitted args); consider dropping None-valued keys.

payload.title: JiraToolkit templates: jira_list_templates exposes templates_dir path; convention candidates not name-validated
payload.body: jiratoolkit.py: (1) jira_list_templates returns 'templates_dir': str(self.templates_dir), an absolute filesystem path visible to the LLM; spec AC13 says 'never paths' for names but the spec's own signature includes templates_dir. Decide whether to return a boolean instead. (2) _validate_template_name is applied only to an explicit template=; project/issuetype flow into convention candidates unvalidated. Jinja's split_template_path rejects '..' segments so it is not exploitable today, but apply the validation to candidates as defence in depth. (3) jira_create_issue runs _validate_issue_type (a Jira read) before rendering, so missing-variable/unknown-template errors on create happen after one read request (no write); spec AC8 says 'before any Jira request'. Either relax the spec wording to 'write request' or render first and re-resolve the issue type.

payload.title: Path traversal via WS locale in Narrator.__init__ (CodeQL 223/224; 225-227 need locale validation to clear)
payload.body: GitHub code scanning alerts 223-227 (py/path-injection, high) on main @42376abda. Taint source: audio_ws.py:601 'locale = data.get("locale", "en")' from the raw WebSocket start_session payload, used unvalidated. REAL GAP (alerts 223/224): Narrator.__init__ (engine.py:118-122) builds self._dir / loc / 'narration.yaml' per locale_chain candidate and reads+yaml.safe_loads it with NO containment check — a locale like '../../../../x' reads any narration.yaml outside the templates dir (CWE-22, constrained to that filename). ALREADY GUARDED (alerts 225/226/227): lexicon.py load_locale_document resolves and checks is_relative_to(base) since 256f9e8ba, but CodeQL does not model that barrier, so the alerts stay open. Fix: validate the locale format at the source (strict regex over locale_chain candidates, e.g. ^[A-Za-z]{2,3}([-_][A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$, reject/fallback to 'en' otherwise) AND add the same resolve+is_relative_to guard in Narrator.__init__ for parity; then dismiss 225-227 on GitHub if the scanner still flags the guarded lines.

payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/schema/models.py:9 does `from parrot.bots.database.models import TableMetadata` at module level. Chain: wiki.cli:64 -> federation.py:46 -> project.py:31 -> schema/models.py:9 -> parrot/bots/__init__.py:10 -> bots/abstract.py:20/25, which loads navconfig and parrot.conf. Two FEAT-540 gates are therefore xfail with reason strings naming that line: test_import_ceilings.py[wiki.cli] and test_graph_tree_imports.py::test_blocker_default_cli_entry_and_plain_ops. Related eager parrot.bots.database.* imports (same family, not caught by the forbidden-prefix list): wiki/schema/producers/ddl.py:12, wiki/schema/render.py:13, wiki/schema/service.py:11, wiki/schema/producers/live.py:9-11 (BigQuery/Postgres/SQL toolkits at module level). Fix: make TableMetadata (and the producer toolkit imports) lazy / TYPE_CHECKING or move the model to a framework-free module, then remove the two xfail marks. Handoff: sdd/state/FEAT-540/handoff-541.md.

payload.title: Review TASK-4333
Wiki SDK MCP transport is not framework-free on the real path (descriptors built from framework tool objects)
payload.body: FEAT-540 review finding. create_wiki_mcp_server(root, transport="sdk") -> build_wiki_tools -> abuild_wiki_tools unconditionally imports create_wiki_tools (parrot_tools.wiki.tools via the wiki/tools.py shim) and parrot.tools.obsidian for vaults; transport.py build_operation_descriptors reads tool._store/_service etc. from the framework tool objects, the reverse of the spec's design (descriptors from the op_* registry + stores). The comment at mcp_server.py:~259-262 claiming wrappers are reconstructed only for the framework transport is false; to_framework_tools is dead code. test_mcp_transport_selector.py only exercises to_sdk_server with a synthetic descriptor, so the AC (SDK local/proxy smoke with parrot.mcp, parrot.tools, parrot_tools blocked) is not actually verified on a real project root. Fix: build descriptors from the op registry, wrap into framework tools only for the framework transport, add a blocked-import test with a real root. Also: mcp_server.py create_* wrap the StdioMCPServer construction inside the ImportError try (auto mode); narrow it to the imports.

payload.title: GraphIndexLoader _CapturingPersistence hides backend capabilities (incremental/embeddings) and leaks connections
payload.body: FEAT-540 review finding. loaders/graphindex.py:~38-52 wraps the persistence in _CapturingPersistence which forwards only persist_graph/replace_document_slice, but builder.py (~250, ~505) now gates on isinstance(self.persistence, IncrementalPersistence/EmbeddingPersistence): with GraphIndexLoader(backend="postgres"|"sqlite") incremental is_stale skipping and upsert_embeddings are silently disabled; no close()/file_hashes. Fix: __getattr__ delegation / explicit forwarding, or pass the capture hook to the builder. Leaks: loaders/graphindex.py:~140-160 _make_persistence opens a new AsyncDB connection per build_graph and never closes persistence; persist_arango.py:~850-872 create_arango_persistence(arango_params=...) opens a client that ArangoPersistence.close() (no-op) never closes; wiki/runtime.py:~71 and wiki/cli.py (_sync_memory_to_graph, _extract_into_graph, audit) never close persistence_for_project results; graphindex/factory.py does not close persistence if a later step raises. Fix with try/finally close and make create_arango_persistence own its client.

payload.title: SourceCollectionManager sqlite/json paths now go through asyncio.run per call (perf + loop side effects), dead Arango duplicates left in sources.py
payload.body: FEAT-540 review finding (TASK-4326). knowledge/wiki/sources.py: every manager call now goes _backend.<op> -> _run_async(coro) = asyncio.run per call (ThreadPoolExecutor + new loop inside a running loop). Measured 300 get_source on sqlite: 0.12s sync (~0.4ms/call), 0.71s inside a running loop (~2.4ms/call); no baseline comparison. After any sync call asyncio.get_event_loop() raises "There is no current event loop" in the main thread (likely related to existing baseline failures). Classes are monkeypatched after the class body with _legacy_* aliases (~1534-1612) and the old Arango _async_*/_arango_* code remains as dead duplicates next to ArangoSourceBackend (TASK-4326 also needed a fix restoring _ARANGO_SOURCES_COLLECTION). Arango behaviour change: _entry_to_doc stores model_dump() (adds destination, decision_source, charter_version, composite_score) where only 12 fields were persisted. Fix: sync-capable backend protocol so sqlite/json call sync implementations directly (or make the manager async), delete dead duplicates, decide the Arango field set explicitly.

payload.title: FEAT-540 review follow-ups: mixin dialect wiring, config precedence/default drifts, stale docstrings
payload.body: Lower-severity FEAT-540 review findings. (1) ontology/mixin.py:~226 builds OntologyIntentResolver without dialect=; pass dialect=self._ont_graph_store.dialect so non-AQL stores do not get AQL dynamic queries rejected with QueryDialectMismatch (TASK-4329 promised dialect-aware resolver). (2) graphindex/pg_schema.py:~110-126 GRAPHINDEX_PG_DSN still falls back to parrot.conf.default_dsn but resolve_pg_settings().dsn / create_graph_persistence("postgres") no longer do (ValueError for environments relying on the default); confirm intent. (3) wiki/cli.py:588 and wiki/llm_resolve.py:17 _env_setting precedence flipped navconfig-first -> environment-first; docstring still old. (4) wiki/project.py:222-231 backend field description says "not validated against the registry" but validators now check it. (5) loaders/graphindex.py:~200 and graphindex/loader _resolve_arango default host 127.0.0.1 while wiki resolve_arango_params dropped implicit loopback: inconsistent. (6) ontology/intent.py: an LLM answering with the old "aql" key is silently ignored (extra=ignore) -> vector_only. (7) ontology/graph_store.py key_field now validated by _literal_attribute: hyphenated key fields now raise ValueError (hardening, behaviour change). (8) knowledge/wiki/tools.py __all__ includes private _EXPORTS; stale GraphIndexPersistence mentions in docstrings of persist_postgres.py, persist_sqlite.py, publish.py. (9) tests/knowledge/test_import_ceilings.py writes artifacts/logs/FEAT-540-import-ceilings.json on every run (UPDATE_EVIDENCE=0 disables). (10) to_sdk_server: verify Server.call_tool accepts a returned CallToolResult against the pinned mcp range (mcp>=1.28.1,<2).
